The results of this study indicate that EWOM partially has a positive effect on intention. Interaction has a positive effect on intention.

articleTitle: An Information System Analysis and Design of Monitoring and Evaluation for Productive Credit Distribution at PT. Bank XYZ
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Monitoring and evaluations aspects are very important for banks and related with the three main functions of bank as agent of trust, agent of development, and agent of service. PT Bank XYZ has problems in monitoring report process and evaluation on productive credit distribution is still manually, report action plan monitoring system from credit analysis still using paper form, recommendation process from head office has not been documented and action plan scheduling by credit analysis still uses whatsapp. The purposes of this research are to design a productive credit distribution dashboard system, reporting system for credit collecting process, headquarter recommendation feature, and feature of credit action plan for collecting activity. The scope of this research only focuses on analysis and design, for the implementation and deployment step not included in this research. Analysis method used is waterfall model method and design method used in this research is UML diagram. The result of this research is the availability of credit distribution information in executive dashboard, reporting system that provides activities by credit analysis during visits to customers, the availability of recommendation delivery regarding productive credit handling by head office and assist the scheduling process of action plan regarding the recommendation.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Information System in the Import Process and Production in the Company with A Case Study at PT.XYZ
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: PT XYZ, a chemical distribution company with large-scale production and high demand, faces several challenges in the production and import process management. These challenges include the unavailability of data on the status of ongoing production and import processes, misplaced import licenses, and lack of information on production and import transactions. These conditions caused difficulties in monitoring the operation of production and imports, which led to significant production performance delays. Therefore, the implementation of an information system is needed to solve these problems and this research aims to analyze and design a suitable information system for the import process and production reports at PT XYZ. The research method used is a case study using interviews and direct observation at the company. In the context of information system design, there is the use of the Unified Modeling Language (UML) method, an effective tool for modeling, designing, and documenting software systems. The results of this research generate a User Interface design that not only speeds up the import process, improves performance efficiency, and helps optimize other business processes for PT XYZ, but also provides more value to the company.

articleTitle: Integrating Eye-Tracking Insights with User Feedback: A UX Evaluation of Website Landing Page
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study investigates the correlation between eye-tracking metrics and user feedback to evaluate user experience (UX) design effectiveness on website landing pages. Utilizing a mixed-methods approach, we examined the interactions of users with three distinct versions of a website landing page, each designed with varying UX principles. Eye-tracking data provided objective insights into users’ visual attention and engagement, while traditional questionnaires captured subjective user perceptions and preferences. Our analysis reveals significant correlations between eye-tracking metrics, such as fixation duration and gaze patterns, with users’ subjective feedback on usability and aesthetic appeal. These findings highlight the potential of integrating eye-tracking technology with user feedback to enhance the design and evaluation process of website landing pages, offering valuable insights for UX researchers and practitioners aiming to optimize digital interfaces for improved user engagement and satisfaction.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing the Satisfaction of Live Commerce Purchasers in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The research objective was to study the factors influencing the satisfaction of live commerce (L-commerce) buyers in Thailand, focusing on perceived visibility, real-time interactivity, security/privacy, order quality, and delivery. The study focused on university students in Pathum Thani province, Thailand. It gathered responses from 363 participants through survey questions. Most respondents were female, aged 20, with monthly expenses ranging from 10,001 to 20,000 baht. On average, they made purchases via live commerce platforms 3–5 times per month. The values of the products purchased per transaction ranged from 0 to 500 baht. The research employed descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis. The findings unveiled those factors such as security/privacy, order quality, delivery, and real-time interactivity positively impacted the satisfaction of live commerce buyers in Thailand, reaching statistical significance at the. 01 level. The outcomes of this investigation hold potential benefits for business organizations. The findings should be used to develop and improve services in various fields to increase consumer satisfaction in purchasing products through live commerce.

articleTitle: Vision-Based Drug Classification System Using Transfer Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Dispensing generic drugs instead of original drugs from pharmacies may cause adverse drug events to patients. It is difficult to separate between generic drugs and originals due to their similarities, except for imprints on the tablets. In this paper, a vision-based medicine tablets classification system using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with a transfer learning approach is proposed. The proposed classification system aims to helps its user distinguish between the original drugs and generic drugs based on imprints on the medicine tablets. Multiple CNN models are created and tested as the classifier for the drug classification system. Three well-known CNN models are chosen as base models for creating CNNs with the transfer learning, including VGG16, Inception-V3, and ResNet50-V2. The developed CNN models are tested with images of medicine tablet taken from smartphones. Results from the experiments are evaluated through accuracies, precisions, recalls, and F-1 scores. Experimental results show satisfying performances of the proposed system in classifying original drugs and generic drugs using visual information.

articleTitle: Probing the Triggers of Online Impulsive Buying in Fashion E-Commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Online impulse buying has become a common phenomenon in consumer behavior, especially through e-commerce platforms in the fashion industry. This phenomenon reflects the tendency of customers to make hasty decisions about what to buy and is often triggered by emotional factors. This study aims to investigate whether online impulse purchases in fashion businesses are influenced by shopping motivation factors and visual merchandising. This research method uses a quantitative approach, by collecting primary data obtained from questionnaires filled out online by 150 respondents who had made online purchases at certain fashion businesses. To determine the significance of each aspect's influence, data analysis was done using coefficient applications. Multiple Linear Regression Analysis is used as a further step to determine the strength of the relationship and the total effect of all the factors on the dependent variable. The research results show that three aspects of shopping motivation and visual merchandising directly influence online impulse buying.

articleTitle: WEB-Based Veterinary Clinic with e-Mail and SMS Notification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: After several decades of development, Electronic Medical Records (EMRs) are now exerting a more significant impact on healthcare practices than ever before. Although most of the reasons for implementing EMRs focus on improving medical care as a whole, one must also consider the effects increased EMR use may have at the level of the patient-physician encounter. In this paper, EMR use with respect to the patient-physician relationship, are examined in the field of veterinary medicine in the Philippines. In such particular situation, the study looked at veterinarian's activities that are confidential such as treating illness and wound in an animal and to operate surgery under a registered veterinarian and along with the determined EMRs needed to be in place for effective treatment. By implementation of an essential system to the development of effective animal health, tracking of scheduling wherein the client will know on what their next appointment is, and to provide a database for storing, updating, and archiving of client's records. This system provides an information system that will help the client's pet to know the basics on how to take good care of their pets.

articleTitle: Use of Google Translate in Chinese-Indonesian Travel Word Translation: Evaluation of Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study examines the application of Google Translate in translating travel-related vocabulary from Indonesian to Chinese. The primary focus is to evaluate the accuracy of these translations using a sample of 90 sentences. The study employs a descriptive methodology to evaluate the accuracy of Google Translate in translating Indonesian travel terminology into Chinese. The assessment results offer crucial insights into the pros and cons of using Google Translate for translating travel terms from Indonesian to Chinese. Based on this research, it was found that translation using Google Translate is clearly faster and more efficient, but there are still several obstacles, especially in terms of translating certain vocabulary, such as place names. Understanding the accuracy of these translations is crucial for several demographics, including travelers, tourism service providers, and language specialists.

articleTitle: Sequential Anaerobic Treatment and Bio-Granules Horizontal Flow Trickling Filter System for Producing Nutrient Solution from Household Wastewater
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The main source of wastewater in Thailand is the daily activities and occupations of its people. Each person produces about 150 liters of household wastewater per day, which is released into the environment. This study aimed to develop treatment methods for household or domestic wastewater that reduce waste and allow its reuse as nutrient for plant. The wastewater was treated with a hybrid anaerobic system and a bio-granule horizontal flow trickling filter, which produced a nutrient solution. The solution had 0.0083 mmol/L of NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, 9.3530 mmol/L of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, 0.0224 mmol/L of PO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and 0.9180 mmol/L of K—essential nutrients for plants. A statistical analysis, using an Independent Samples T-Test, showed that the average values of NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> and NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> in the nutrient solution were not significantly different from those in a standard nutrient solution with 12 formulas. This nutrient solution was used to grow three types of salad greens (red oak, green oak, and cos lettuce) in a hydroponic system with clay pebbles. The results showed that the wastewater treatment methods could produce a plant nutrient solution that would benefit both communities and the agricultural sector of the country.

articleTitle: Analysis of Consumer Purchasing Decision Indicators Using Decision Tree Algorithm to Create Competitive Advantage Strategies for Resep Nini Uti
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: From year to year, business competition in various types of businesses becomes increasingly fierce. Companies are encouraged to create competitive advantage strategies to stand out from competitors and survive in the market. This research aims to help a small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) business in Indonesia that sells ready-to-eat food product, Resep Nini Uti, to create competitive advantage strategies by utilizing the insights of consumer purchasing decision indicators. The research method used is data analytics using the CRISP-DM model with the decision tree algorithm in the RapidMiner application. The results show that the primary indicators in consumer purchasing decisions for Resep Nini Uti are sales method variety, packaging design, product taste, and similar competitors’ products. The high accuracy of the decision tree model (90%) validates these findings. This research concludes that Resep Nini Uti should focus on implementing several strategies to create a competitive advantage and win the competition in the market. The strategies are optimizing an omnichannel strategy, creating several attractive packaging designs, implementing quality control, and innovating products continuously.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation of Open Data of Government Website: A Case Study Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Open data is closely related to government, supporting transparency and accountability. The paper focus on DKI Jakarta government's open data website, which this website provides an accurate, open, centralized, and integrated database for e-government. This research will use three tools to help collect information for evaluation purpose. First is the Web Accessibility Evaluation tool (WAVE) which will help identify accessibility errors and the web content accessibility guideline. Then the second is the Webpage Test to analyze the website network and speed of loading when accessing the website. And the third use VisualEyes to see how attractive and clear the website is. The aim of this research is to identify the errors and malfunctions that occur and do not affect user comfort when accessing and improving the quality of the site in future. From the results of this research using WAVE, there is still a color contrast between the background and text, and some small errors were found. For now, the website's loading is quite fast, only 8.40 seconds, and the results from VisualEyes are quite high that is 77%, where the website is sufficient to be clear and aesthetically appealing.

articleTitle: Applying the Monodzukuri Concept to Find Standard Values for Machine Installation Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This paper showed the application of the Monodzukuri concept to find standard values for machine installation conditions (Pipes animal feed). Smartphone technology, QR codes, and Google Sheets were applied to collect data following the Monodzukuri concept. These technologies help workers do work easier, faster, and more conveniently. The trial and error method was used, and its result was analyzed using an Excel program. This experiment gives the standard values for machine installation: Pipe 1 has a speed of 9 rpm and air volume of 0.4 m/s, Pipe 2 has a speed of 20 rpm and air volume of 0.2 m/s, and Pipe 3 has a speed of 24 rpm and air volume 0.2 m/s, respectively. Moreover, the standard values were used in the production process and rechecked for correction by the I-MR control chart via the Minitab program.

articleTitle: Detection of Waste Cooking Oil Quality Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Low-quality cooking oil can have negative health impacts when consumed continuously. The quality of cooking oil can be determined through various quality assessment procedures. In today's era, there are many technologies utilizing Artificial Intelligence to facilitate decision-making, one of which is the use of fuzzy logic methods. Previously, testing the quality of cooking oil was done manually by the community. This research aims to implement a system for testing the quality of waste cooking oil using fuzzy logic. This helps in determining whether the waste cooking oil is still suitable for consumption. The study also adopts a prototype approach in the design and development of an application that integrates with the fuzzy logic method. The research involves testing using several samples of waste cooking oil. After obtaining data on parameters such as peroxide value, acid number, and water content, this data is processed using fuzzy logic to obtain classification results. The testing has shown that all outputs produced align with the fuzzy rules or predefined rules. This indicates that the system can operate very well in detecting input and generating outputs that are appropriate for assessing the quality of waste cooking oil.

articleTitle: User Experience Evaluation of Pension Fund Application Using System Usability Scale and Heuristic Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Identification letters serve as a vital tool for pension fund companies to disburse pension payments to eligible individuals. The evolution of identification letters from paper-based to digital forms, aimed to simplify data verification for participants. However, the implementation of this digital solution has met with resistance from participants, as evidenced by complaints on the Google Play platform. This study delves into the user experience of the identification letters application, seeking to identify areas for improvement. Employing the System Usability Scale (SUS) and Heuristic Evaluation methods, the study reveals that while the application's SUS score of 72 indicates overall satisfaction among users, the HE score of 47 highlights significant usability issues. The findings underscore the need for pension fund companies to prioritize user experience in developing identification letter applications. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of User Experience research methods and provides valuable insights for enhancing pension fund services.

articleTitle: Preserving Perak's Cultural Legacy: Advancing Heritage Conservation Through Immersive 360° Visual Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The investigation of the rock art in Tambun Cave in Perak serves as evidence of the area's cultural legacy, emphasizing the importance of conservation. This concept paper explores the integration of Augemented Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR) technologies, led by the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), to preserve this valuable heritage. The study derives insights from an interview with a solitary expert in rock art archaeology who has extensive knowledge of Perak's ancient cave arts. The interview focuses on four key themes: Cultural Heritage Knowledge, Cultural Heritage Experience, Cultural Data Sources, and Cultural Heritage Information Perception. This study aims to assess the feasibility and public response to the utilization of AR and VR technologies for the purpose of conserving cultural assets. By employing the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and drawing on the expertise of a trained archaeologist, this study evaluates individuals’ attitudes and perceptions towards these technologies, with a specific emphasis on the highlighted themes. The objective is to thoroughly examine these aspects in the context of incorporating AR and VR technology to preserve Tambun Cave's rock art, eventually to create a strong and comprehensive policy to preserve Perak's cultural heritage, ensuring long-term protection and recognition of these important artworks.

articleTitle: Piloting Virtual Studio Along with Marker-Based Augmented Reality Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: To go beyond today's media capabilities, this study explores the application of Marker-based Augmented Reality (AR) technology in virtual studio settings, particularly in the context of a news studio. The study utilizes various open-source tools such as Unreal Engine, Blender, and OBS. In Unreal Engine, an approach in which a tracking system is used by a virtual camera and blueprint is also mentioned. An AR application is created using Unity and the Vuforia Engine, while 3D content is developed in Blender. This approach introduces a novel framework for creating immersive and interactive media experiences, demonstrating the effective application of AR in a virtual studio, and opening new possibilities for media production. The system is applied across different news segments, including sports, flood disasters, and crime reports, enabling interactive experiences with varied 3D content. Although AR is a technology that helps humans enhance interest, stimulate engagement, and potentially improve learning, the study points out the possibility of an increased workload. This paper uses the subjective workload assessment tool NASA-TLX for the questionnaires, and in-depth interviews are also conducted to provide insights. The results demonstrate how AR could potentially enrich the overall experience.

articleTitle: Achieving Customer Engagement Through Exposing Brand Expertise on Social Media – Toward Online Visual Merchandising
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This paper aims to study how a traditional woven fabric company implements its social media marketing strategic actions and investigate how social media customer experience can affect customer engagement. The study focuses on the communication tactic through utilization of social media content that holds the objective to leverage the brand expertise. This study uses a quantitative survey method among 105 Indonesian consumers’ sample. The study offers a novel contribution to the research on enhancing social media customer engagement behavior through social media customer experience resulting from content about brand expertise. This paper suggests that social media customer experience tends to affect positively three social media customer engagement behaviors: liking, commenting, and sharing. The findings give some hints to traditional woven fabric retailers on how to drive social media customer engagement in order to drive their online visual merchandising’ outcomes.

articleTitle: Decision Tree for Boosting Firewall Accuracy: Optimizing Action Classification for Enhanced Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to categorize many “actions” types presented in the comprehensive dataset, known as “Internet Firewall Data.” We employed this dataset to train and assess several models, including KNN, NB, RF, DL, and DT, aiming to identify a highly accurate classification model for firewall log data. Through 10-fold cross-validation, we determined that the RF and DT models achieved robust performance, with accuracies of 99.86% and 99.85%, respectively. Moreover, the NB and DT models exhibited the quickest processing times, measured at 0.22 s and 0.35 s, respectively. These findings underscore the substantial impact of reducing the number of “actions” on the model's capacity for discernment and precision. This paper offers insights and recommendations valuable to both cybersecurity professionals and researchers, advocating for the consolidation of firewall action groups to enhance manageability. Simplifying firewall configurations not only bolsters security but also diminishes operational complexities.

articleTitle: Features Online Food Delivery and Online Reviews in Generating Satisfaction and Consumer Behavioral Intentions
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The emergence of technology has dramatically enhanced the flexibility of consumers’ lifestyles, including using Online Food Delivery (OFD) applications. However, optimizing delivery accuracy for a more satisfactory experience is crucial. This study examines and identifies consumers’ behavioral intentions using OFD applications through various factors, such as perceived control and online tracking, food quality, online reviews, and overall satisfaction. The study involved 409 users of online food ordering applications in Greater Jakarta, Indonesia, selected through a purposive sampling method. Data was collected through questionnaires distributed via social media and analyzed using the partial least square structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) method. The results indicate that perceived control, online tracking, food quality, and online reviews significantly impact overall satisfaction, positively influencing consumers’ intention to continue using OFD applications. This research provides valuable insights into consumer behavior and satisfaction in online food ordering applications, particularly in evaluating application features, food quality, and online reviews.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Electronic Circuits Diagram Using Computer Vision Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The researcher has experience in the electronics field. In their work Failure Analysis to better understand Failure Analysis work, The reference describes work that is similar to work in the Failure Analysis [1]. They often encounter circuit diagrams in the form of PDF files or pictures, which they use reference circuits to illustrate electronic component attributes and standardize symbols [2], to analyze their work. Most reference circuits are in PDF format. However, analyzing electronic circuits can be time-consuming and challenging, especially the obtained accuracy of electronic values. This research proposes using computer vision and image processing to calculate electronic circuits from images, which reduces time and increases accuracy in analyzing electronic circuits. Analyzing electronic analysis theory is also shown through this reference [3]. This research aims to decrease the time required to analyze electronic circuits and enhance the accuracy of electronic values obtained from image analysis. Computer vision and image processing technologies are being used to accomplish this goal. To understand image processing principles, this reference explains relevant theories [4] [5]. The methodology involves preprocessing images or PDF files to extract data for the main process. The main process utilizes object detection, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) training, and Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to identify the types of electronic components in the circuit. The reference explains CNN principles studied to improve research efficiency [6]. This research shows that the analysis time is significantly reduced compared to manually creating circuits using simulation programs. Furthermore, the accuracy of the analysis is evaluated against manual analysis by humans and the time taken from the start of circuit creation to obtaining analysis values. This method significantly reduces the time required to analyze circuits from images to electronic values and identifies any components within the circuit. As a result, this research contributes to making electronic circuit analysis more efficient and rapid in the electronics field.

articleTitle: Information System Strategy Planning at PT Pelayaran Nasional Indonesia (PT Pelni)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: PT Pelni is a state-owned enterprise engaged in transportation, logistics, and marine tourism in which some components support the operations, namely the IT operations Department. The problems faced by the department include, there is no activity for monitoring applications, data centers, and IT helpdesk ticketing, there is no display of tickets that are being processed and completed, and the application and data center information only show the overall details. This study aims to analyze the strategy of information systems and information technology proposals that can help organizations. The methodology that used is Ward and Peppard to answer the problems, an analysis of the internal and external environment was carried out with SWOT analysis, balanced scorecard, critical success factor, and gap analysis. There are several findings from the results of the analysis obtained, namely an increase in the number of tickets and the addition of IT human resources. The results of the analysis were able to identify the strategic needs of the IS in the operational department of PT Pelni. The resulting proposal is a monitoring dashboard which is presented in the form of a user interface that contains information about application conditions, data centers, and IT helpdesk performance.

articleTitle: Driving Watching Intention and eWoM Through Social Media Engagement Toward Movie Ad Trailer
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Shaped by digitalization and behavior changes, the entertainment industry currently relies heavily on over the top (OTT) platforms for on-demand streaming. This study investigates the OOT landscape, focusing on movie promotion through social media and the impact of trailers on viewer intentions. Global OTT users are projected to surge, led by Indonesia in Southeast Asia. Emphasizing the critical role of social media engagement, the study highlights the importance of distinct and credible movie trailers. Theoretical foundations, encompassing movie trailer believability, involvement with movie trailer, social media engagement, electronic word of mouth and watching intention, guide the research, addressing gaps in understanding viewer behavior on OTT platforms. The results show that involvement with movie trailer is positively related to social media engagement, movie trailer believability does not have positive relationship with social media engagement, social media engagement is positively related to eWoM, and social media engagement is positively related to watching intention. The research offers valuable insights for marketers navigating the evolving OTT environment.

articleTitle: Intention to Use Virtual Reality in Tourism
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: To attain sustainable tourism, the authorities responsible for tourist development have employed sophisticated technology to promote places, entice visitors, and safeguard the environment. Hence, it is crucial to acknowledge that the current academic research on tourism technologies has demonstrated that virtual reality (VR) has a substantial impact on the inclination of prospective tourists to visit a particular location. However, it is worth mentioning that there needs to be more research exploring the cognitive and sensory processes that individuals undergo when engaging with VR technology. Therefore, this study utilizes a methodology to evaluate the readability of questionnaires, including validity and reliability assessments. The survey comprises a total of 21 items, which cover eight specific areas of inquiry. These areas include social influence, performance expectation, effort expectation, facilitating conditions, virtual reality satisfaction, telepresence, and visit intention. Participants were directed to express their responses using a Likert scale that spanned from 1 to 5, where 1 represented a significant disagreement and 5 represented a strong agreement. The study's results encompassed a sample size of 182 respondents, with a substantial representation from several regions, including Greater Jakarta, Central Java, East J ava, and West Java. The data will be analyzed using statistical software packages such as SPSS and SmartPLS. This study emphasizes the importance of virtual reality as a highly effective marketing tool for promoting destinations. It enhances the current corpus of VR tourism literature by providing theoretical insights and practical expertise.

articleTitle: A Time-Focused Approach to Crime Prediction: An Analysis in Seoul
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to create effective prediction models for crimes that occur infrequently or in regions with low crime frequency when considering temporal aspects in crime prediction methods. We estimated the effects of time-varying and a priori ascertainable factors such as day of the week, special day, and weather, while detecting abnormal trends that cannot be captured by these factors, and combine them into crime prediction. However, as crime data is often imbalanced with very few positive examples, and the estimation of parameters becomes difficult when the data is subdivided spatiotemporally, we challenged this issue by dividing the city into spatial clusters with high socioeconomic and physical homogeneity and conducting the analysis for each cluster. Validated for two types of crime: simple assault and sexual offense, and obtained better prediction performance than the benchmark, especially for the latter.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Water Quality Monitoring System in Philippine Off-Grid Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Contaminated and polluted water poses significant threats to human health, necessitating vigilant monitoring of water sources for potential contamination. This paper introduces a low-cost Internet of Things (IoT)-based water quality monitoring system designed to address water quality challenges in rural communities, as demonstrated through a case study conducted in the Philippines. The system consists of two core components. The hardware component of the system, built on Arduino technology and featuring real-time data transmission, focuses on monitoring pH levels, turbidity, and temperature via sensors. The system is equipped to transmit data to a cloud database and send informative messages to mobile numbers, updating users on the status of water supplies. The application component acts as a user interface for accessing and managing data collected by the sensors. The successful deployment of this Water Quality Monitoring (WQM) system not only helps community leaders and health workers monitor water sources but also underscores its potential to empower communities in safeguarding their water sources, thereby contributing to the advancement of clean and safe water access.

articleTitle: Spot Unconscious Biases by Using Digital Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Identifying blind spots caused by unconscious biases remains challenging. Although advanced virtual technologies have eliminated physical limits, psychological barriers still prevent people from naturally embracing diversity, equality, inclusiveness, and emotional connection. The world is inviting diverse cultures, groups, people, approaches, attitudes, projects, and so on to improve positive inclusivity, yet unconscious prejudices create blind spots that undermine quality. Identifying, and eliminating such blind spots is critical for improving fairness in businesses, education, law, politics, and other professions. Using qualitative and experimental research the researchers proposed digital tool “Identify Unconscious Biases (i-UnBias)” evaluates emotional engagement to predict unconscious biases in real-life or assessment-based environments. Identifying unconscious biases can aid in critical and delicate decision-making processes and help in diagnosing an individual's severe emotional condition (suicidal thoughts, sadness, overconfidence, etc.). The i-UnBias tool will serve as a prophylactic strategy for risks caused by unconscious bias. This tool was tested on 25 people and scores has a substantial association with assessment-based unconscious bias scores. The research contributes to the use of digital technology for social development and current business management sectors such as risk management, human resources, business development, entrepreneurship, and global business in general by detecting and eliminating or reducing unconscious bias.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency in Manufacturing Process on CNC Machine - A SME Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study focuses on optimizing the use of a coolant pump to clean the CNC machine holder while conserving electrical energy. Coolant pumps serve several functions, including cleaning, lubrication, and cooling. There are three types of cooling pumps available for CNC machines such as shower coolant, through spindle coolant, and bed flushing coolant. The bed flushing coolant pump is responsible for cleaning the engine mount of metal scraps. However, this pump is always running, even when the machine is on standby or not in production activity, leading to unnecessary energy waste. The goal of this research is to improve energy efficiency by optimizing the bed flushing coolant pump with TRIZ design analysis. The approach involves adding a timer-based adaptive program to automatically turn off the bed flushing coolant pump 60 seconds after the production process is complete or when the machine is not in operation. Based on the six-month implementation, there has been a significant saving of electrical energy in the CNC of 936 kWh, which equates to a reduction in energy consumption of 12.5%.

articleTitle: Determining Factors of the Intention to Use Digital Banking
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study examines the determining factors of the customer's intention to use digital banks. Interest rates and cost value were examined to analyze customer intention to use digital banking. This study uses the theory of planned behavior to analyze factors determined of customer intention to use digital banks. This study used 150 data from an online questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS software version 4. The results showed that interest rates and cost value positively and significantly affected of using digital banking. Attractive interest rates and components of cost value, namely ease of transactions, minimal costs, and complete service features, encourage individual intention to use digital banks. The implication of this study is digital bank companies should keep the interest rate and cost value more competitive with conventional banks. The digital bank should maintain a good relationship with customers through innovation in IT, good interest rates, and complete banking features that give customers additional advantages, increase trust, and also minimizing risk to customers.

articleTitle: Factors Affecting EFL Learners' Anxieties in English Speaking
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The study's objectives were 1) to investigate factors affecting EFL learners” anxieties in English speaking in three aspects: Learner Factor, Teaching and Learning Factor, and Family Factor 2) to compare factors affecting EFL learners” anxieties in English speaking in three aspects based on students” faculty and gender, and 3) to compile additional suggestions. 420 Thai-Nichi Institute of Technology (TNI) students from the second semester of the 2023 academic year served as research samples, which were originated from simple random sampling technique. The open-ended questionnaire and the rating scale were the tools utilized to collect the data. The data were analyzed using the following statistics: frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation, t-test, f-test., and content analysis. The findings were as follows: 1) Factors affecting EFL learners” anxieties in English speaking were at moderate level. After considering each aspect, it was discovered that Learner Factor and Teaching and Learning Factor were at moderate level, while Family Factor was at low level. 2) The students with different genders pointed out that there were significant differences. When considering each aspect, all aspects showed statistically significant differences at. 05 level. 3) The students with different faculties showed statistically significant differences in overall at. 05. When considering each aspect, it was found that there were statistically significant differences at. 05 level in all aspects; Learner Factor, Teaching and Learning Factor, and Family Factor. Additionally, there were 2 pairs of different faculties in Learner Factor and Teaching and Learning Factor. There was 1 pair of different faculties in Family Factor. 4) Further recommendations from Thai-Nichi Institute of Technology (TNI) students were as follows: the students struggle to come up with proper vocabulary while they are speaking English, the students experience nervousness when speaking in public in English, and the students concern about Grammar mistakes when they speak English.

articleTitle: Analysis of Hospitalization-Recovery Duration for DHF Patients at RSUD Haji, East Java Utilizing the Three-Parameter Log-Logistic Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Analytical challenges such as skewness and asymmetry often arise with continuous data, especially when values are strictly positive, rendering traditional models like the Normal distribution ineffective. Addressing these issues, this study introduces the Three-Parameter Log-Logistic Regression (LL3R) model, an advancement of the Three-Parameter Log-Logistic Distribution (LL3D). This research aims to apply the LL3R model to estimate parameters and test hypotheses, specifically analyzing hospitalization duration for Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever patients in 2022 at RSUD Haji, East Java Province. The response variable is the duration of hospitalization until recovery, with 10 predictor variables considered. The model's parameters are estimated using Conjugate Gradient (CG) and Berndt-Hall-Hall-Hausman (BHHH) technique for numerical iteration. Hypothesis testing employs the LRT test. Model effectiveness is gauged via the AICc. Results indicate the BHHH method outperforms CG with a lower AICc of 124,082 compared to CG's 3450,22 so that the best LL3R model is given by numerical iteration of BHHH method. Simultaneously, testing rejects the null hypothesis, and individual tests reveal significant effects of seven variables including body temperature, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, pulse frequency, respiratory rate, gender, and age on the duration of hospitalization until recovery of DHF patients at a 5% significance level.

articleTitle: Perceived Risk and Untrust in Purchasing Electronic Products on Electronic Commerce
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Information quality is essential in e-commerce because it impacts consumer behavior and customer purchase intentions and helps in the decision-making process. Improving information quality can increase trust, lower purchase risk, and, ultimately, the success of the e-commerce platform. Therefore, this study aims to explore the determining factors in the purchase intention of electronic products in e-commerce. Data collection used a questionnaire distributed to 200 internet users in Indonesia who had transacted in e-commerce, especially purchasing electronic products. Therefore, purposive sampling was established in this study. The data analysis technique used component-based structural equation modeling. The results of this study prove that information quality has a negative and significant effect on perceived risk. Untrust has a positive and significant effect on perceived risk. Information quality has a negative and significant effect on untrust, while purchase intention has a positive and significant effect. Perceived risk and trust have a negative and significant effect on purchase intention. Finally, for the sustainability of e-commerce customers, especially electronic products, sellers must provide accurate information to customers to improve the shopping experience and build customer trust.

articleTitle: Analysis of Classification Models of Firewall Log Data Attacked by Data Poisoning and Evasion Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research explores vulnerabilities in machine learning classification models applied to firewall log data, specifically examining susceptibility to data poisoning and evasion attacks. The main objective is to evaluate the robustness of different algorithms when classifying firewall logs under adversarial conditions. The study assesses each model's accuracy in classifying log actions and introduces deliberate data poisoning and evasion attacks. The results highlight significant variations in model resilience. Notably, the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) demonstrates exceptional performance, maintaining a comparatively accuracy even after being subjected to data poisoning. In contrast, the rest model experiences a substantial drop in accuracy, indicating its vulnerability to such attacks. Additionally, evasion attacks impact model performance differently. Despite the evasion attack, the ANN consistently maintains the same accuracy, showcasing its steadfast nature. Conversely, the rest model witnesses a notable decrease in accuracy after evasion attack especially the decision tree model. These findings provide valuable insights into the comparative resilience of machine learning models against data poisoning and evasion attacks in the context of firewall log classification. The research underscores the importance of selecting robust algorithms to enhance the security of network systems amidst evolving cyber threats.

articleTitle: Comparing the User Experience of Mobile Banking Applications Using System Usability Scale and Usability Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Rapid advancements in information system technologies are crucial for companies, including those in the banking sector, to stay competitive and take a leading position in the market. While many banking companies aim to offer top-notch services through Mobile Banking Apps, some mobile banking apps receive negative reviews despite having a good rating above 4.5 on Google PlayStore. This research aims to measure the usability of two Mobile Banking Apps in Indonesia of BRImo by BRI and BNI Mobile Banking by BNI with the combination of quantitative and qualitative measurement using SUS and usability testing. The test results show that Mobile Banking Apps in Indonesia have different usability scores of 67.5 for BRImo and 66.1 for BNI Mobile Banking. Beside that, BRImo also has a higher score for both effectiveness and efficiency than BNI Mobile Banking with 97.3% vs 96.67% in terms of success rate and 95.48% vs 86.88% in terms of overall relative efficiency. The implication of this research is to contribute to academia on how to implement SUS and Usability Testing methods to measure the usability of mobile apps, and also contribute to Banking industries on how to develop a good Mobile Banking Apps.

articleTitle: Digitizing Rural Enterprise Management in Indonesia: A Design Thinking Paradigm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This project devised a design thinking paradigm to provide guidance for the digital transformation of village-owned firms in Indonesia. The study of firm managers in Sumbersekar village yielded valuable information regarding their current utilization of technology, the difficulties they face, and their requirements for training. The proposed methodology of design thinking, which prioritizes the needs and experiences of individuals, offers a structured approach for creating digital capabilities that are specifically adapted to the limitations and challenges faced by village enterprises. The findings emphasize the significance of employing collaborative participatory methods to develop enterprise digital literacy and online systems. This study provides practical resources to assist rural businesses in utilizing digital technologies to achieve expansion and financial viability.

articleTitle: Exploring the Nexus: Loneliness in Cyberbullying, and Problematic Internet Use in Modern Social Media Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The study examines exploring the nexus: Loneliness in cyberbullying, and problematic internet use in modern social media dynamics. The study applied quantitative method with a total of 121 participants aged 18–25 in Indonesia. Feeling of loneliness were measured using the Social and Emotional Loneliness Scale for Adults (SELSA). Problematic internet use (PIU) was measured using the Generalized Problematic Internet Use Scale 2 (GPIUS2). Both SELSA and GPIUS2 adapted to Indonesian language. Cyberbullying behavior was measured using a cyberbullying scale based on cyberbullying theory. The results of the analysis are: 1) emotional loneliness does not have a direct effect on cyberbullying behavior, 2) social loneliness has a significant direct effect on cyberbullying behavior, and 3) social loneliness also has a significant indirect effect on cyberbullying behavior through the mediation of problematic internet use. Thus, it can be said that loneliness, especially social loneliness, plays a role in predicting cyberbullying behavior with the mediation of problematic internet use.

articleTitle: Virtual Learning Amid COVID-19 in Nigeria: Prospects and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study investigates the benefits of virtual learning experiences in Nigeria post-during the pandemic, emphasizing antecedents such as geographical regions, the impact of the digital divide, recommendations, insights, and primary challenges on student perceptions. Utilizing an exploratory approach with a survey questionnaire, data was collected from a diverse sample of 200 students across educational levels. The results of these preliminary inductive investigations offer valuable perspectives and information that can guide decision-making processes for future academic planning and disaster readiness. The results indicate that different geographical regions and insights significantly influence perceived benefits, while the digital divide, primary challenges, and recommendations may not play a crucial role. Specifically, 51% of respondents find virtual learning content and interactions satisfactory. Additionally, 50% believe virtual learning fosters strong teacher-student bonds, enhancing overall learning efficiency. These findings offer valuable insights and recommendations for policymakers and educators aiming to improve the effectiveness, accessibility, and inclusivity of virtual learning in Nigeria's education system. The study contributes to the existing knowledge on virtual learning, informing decision-making for a more successful and inclusive virtual learning environment in Nigeria.

articleTitle: NFTs and Malaysian Wau Game: A Contemporary Approach to Cultural Heritage Conservation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Cultural heritage is a vital aspect of any society, and it is important to preserve it for future generations. However, traditional methods of cultural preservation have proven to be ineffective in the face of technological advancements and globalization. Blockchain technology, which includes NFTs, has emerged as a promising solution to cultural preservation. The main aim of this study is to investigate the potential of Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs) in the preservation of the Malaysian Wau game cultural heritage. A mixed-methods approach is used in the study, which also includes surveys and interviews with Wau practitioners, NFTs major figures, and NFTs users. As a result of their ability to transfer ownership and control of digital assets in a secure and transparent manner, NFTs have been demonstrated to be a useful instrument for cultural preservation. Yet, there are obstacles to the adoption of NFTs as well, such as the high implementation costs and the requirement for advanced technical knowledge. The study concludes by offering recommendations for the implementation of NFTs in preserving cultural heritage of Malaysian, including the need for collaboration between NFTs stakeholders and the development of clear guidelines and standards assessing their practicality, and proposing strategies for their effective implementation in safeguarding the Malaysian Wau game heritage.

articleTitle: Environmental Concerns and Health Consciousness: Determinants of Consumer Willingness to Buy on E-Grocery Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study investigates consumer behavior towards e-grocery platforms and analyzes how environmental concern, consumer awareness, and health consciousness impact willingness to buy while evaluating the effect of social influences. Using a random sampling approach, we engaged 321 e-grocery users, ensuring a representative and bias-minimized sample. Data were collected through an online survey distributed on digital platforms with an impressive participation rate of 93 %. The survey focused on the attitudes, preferences, and behaviors related to e-grocery shopping. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was applied to explore the relationships between variables. The findings revealed that environmental concerns and health consciousness significantly influence consumers’ willingness to buy, mediated by enhanced consumer awareness. Surprisingly, social influence had no substantial effect on purchase intention. This study enriches the discourse on digital consumer behavior by emphasizing the need for sustainable and health-oriented shopping practices in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Development of Employment Tracking System with File Routing for Human Resource Management for Adamson University
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The research attempts to improve the efficacy and efficiency of the academic institution's HR procedures. The design and implementation of a cutting-edge employment tracking system with file routing methods is the main focus of this work. The system streamlines the hiring, onboarding and personnel management procedures and is customized to fit Adamson University's unique requirements. By incorporating emerging technology, the study tackles issues that the HR department faces and facilitates a smooth exchange of data and documents. The suggested method makes sure that the employee records are tracked accurately and promptly. It also makes it easier for various HR departments to collaborate.

articleTitle: A Study on Student Satisfaction Towards Metaverse Implementation for Language Learning - A Case Study of Binus University Language Department
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Practicum learning using third-party applications such as Zoom, Google Meet, and others has proven unsuitable for long-term results. Previous research suggests an alternative e-learning approach utilizing metaverse-based applications to facilitate pronunciation and communication practicum learning. Recognizing the potential of a metaverse in enhancing learning experiences, BINUS University implemented the use of metaverse for each department in the fall semester of 2023 utilizing an app called “Space-collab”. This case study focuses on the implementation of a metaverse in the language department, specifically in Japanese, Chinese, and English literature for contextual learning purposes. The mixed-method research method is used to employ a questionnaire as one of the data collection methods, supplemented by observation results and interviews conducted in metaverse classes. The majority of student responses indicate neutrality in three aspects: enjoyability, motivation, and reducing anxiety. This can be due to contrasting purposes of utilization between language departments. For example, Japanese literature utilizes metaverse for presentation purposes only while English Literature leverages the space for playing murder case studies resulting in contrasting students' satisfactory experiences across different language departments. The result of this research served as the pioneer research to propose the future implementation of metaverse classes, which is the limitation of this study.

articleTitle: Automated PMI-Based Custom Dictionary for Enhanced Thai Language Tokenization
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Thai language tokenization is challenging due to the lack of explicit word delimiters in Thai script. Our research focuses on processing Thai product names to identify product keywords, which requires improving the tokenization process for specific product names. The existing methods rely on manual custom dictionaries combined with dictionary-based tokenization. These conventional methods are laborious and error-prone, especially when adapting to specific naming conventions. This research proposes an innovative automated custom dictionary method using Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI), tested on a large dataset from Jenbunjerd Co., Ltd. This approach significantly improves the accuracy and performance of tokenization. This PMI-driven approach outperformed conventional methods and aligned more closely with human linguistic decisions, demonstrated through similarity score distributions and reduced in low-scoring matches. This research not only develops Thai NLP but also suggests potential applications of PMI with complex scripts in other languages.

articleTitle: Powering Sales Insights: A Comparative Analysis of Data Visualization Tools, Microsoft Power BI vs Tableau
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Currently, business intelligence is a fundamental technology used in business intelligence applications. Data visualizations facilitate informed decision-making for firms regarding their business plans. To ascertain forthcoming patterns, prospects, and apprehensions, enterprises and organizations must collect, scrutinize, and understand data. Due to the lack of programming language knowledge among some consumers, many professionals face difficulties in selecting the most suitable tools. This impedes the utilization of business intelligence technology. The comparison parameters are deemed unclear and imprecise, as indicated by multiple research studies. The researcher conducted a comprehensive analysis of the comparative study. This research will utilize multiple parameters for comparison. The survey specifically examines Microsoft Power BI and Tableau, which are widely recognized as the most prevalent analytical tools. Both possess the ability to transform unprocessed data into valuable business knowledge. A comparison is made between Power BI and Tableau to determine their suitability for business decision-making. Companies in search of affordable and easy- to-use business intelligence solutions for their employees sought access to the major data sources derived from the company's sales performance in 2022. According to this analysis, Power BI's familiar interface makes it more user-friendly compared to Tableau, which has more intricate features and capabilities.

articleTitle: Predicting the Factors to Artificial Intelligence in Peer-to-Peer Energy Sharing Service Adoption Intention: A Structural Equation Model Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Energy consumption significantly increased in recent decades, notably at the household level, due to economic development, rising population, and technological advancements. To address this sustainability concern, peer-to-peer energy sharing service (P2PESS) is introduced as a solution to household level energy needs. However, P2PESS has yet to be fully explored in terms of development and adoption. As such, this study attempts to provide an understanding of the adoption intention on artificial intelligence (AI) in P2PESS a developing country. This study is realized by developing an extended adoption intention model analyzed through partial-least squares - structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results show that attitude is the most significant predictor of AI in P2PESS adoption intention. This study also reveals that the trust dimension has the strongest effect on attitude, while attitude toward use has the strongest effect on behavioral intention. Also, this study confirms ease of use and usefulness as critical factors in adoption intention. Meanwhile, AI-anxiety is the least significant predictor in the model. Finally, this study is the first evidence of AI in P2PESS adoption intention from the perspective of household level users.

articleTitle: Service Fairness in Fixed Broadband Internet Services and Its Impact on Customer Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Service fairness in fixed broadband internet services is critical to ensure fair resource distribution and a satisfactory user experience. Therefore, this study aims to explore formative service fairness factors and customer value by correlating them with customer outcomes (trust and commitment). This study focused on 343 fixed broadband internet customers in three major cities in Indonesia by administering questionnaires to capture customers' perceptions of service fairness and perceived value. Therefore, a convenience sampling approach was applied in this study. The results have proven that procedural, distributive, and interactional justice are the constructs of service justice in fixed broadband internet services. Service justice in fixed broadband internet services positively and significantly affects customer trust and commitment. In addition, it was also found that customer value also has a positive and significant effect on customer trust and commitment. Finally, trust has a positive and significant effect on customer commitment. This research contributes to fixed broadband internet service providers' development of effective strategies to achieve service justice.

articleTitle: The Intervening Roles of Digitality and Sustainability in the Resilience of Family Businesses
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Disruptive business changes demand business organizations to be resilient. Sustainability management, utilization of digital technology, and relevant leadership approaches are expected factors in establishing family business resilience. This article is an attempt to confirm the impact of leadership, sustainability, and digitality on resilience in family companies. A survey-based study with multivariate analysis was carried out to examine the four hypotheses. The study involved 297 owners and/or managers of family businesses in Jakarta, Indonesia. PLS Structural Equation Modeling was applied to model the perceptual data and SmartPLS version 4.1 was employed. The results explain that leadership has an indirect effect on the resilience of family companies. Digital mastery and sustainability management are essential intervening factors. This article recommends family businesses should align the prosocial leadership of owners and/or managers and/or with digital mastery and sustainability management efforts to leverage of business resilience.

articleTitle: Capsure: A Novel Application of CNNs, OpenAl's Language Model, and Google Text-to-Speech for Reliable Drug Recognition in the Philippines
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study presents the development and evaluation of CapSure, a web-based application designed to facilitate pharmaceutical product identification for individuals in the low-vision community. Using advanced computer vision technology, CapSure accurately classifies pharmaceutical products, providing relevant information to users, thus enhancing their independence and quality of life. The study involved a two-fold evaluation process: a comprehensive performance assessment of the underlying image classification model, and a user-focused survey based on ISO/IEC 25010 software quality standard. The image classification model exhibited an impressive overall accuracy of 98.65%, demonstrating its robustness and effectiveness. A usability survey, administered to 15 participants from the low-vision community, reported high scores across all sub-characteristics of the ISO 25010 standard, validating CapSure's effectiveness and user-friendliness. Future enhancements may include the integration of voice commands and the expansion of the pharmaceutical product database.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Mobile Banking for Indonesian Banking Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research aims to understand the implementation of the UTAUT model in influencing behavioral intentions and usage behavior in using BCA Mobile Banking. The population of this study was 147 BCA Mobile Banking users, and data analysis used SEM PLS. The results of this research show that facilitating conditions affect behavioral intention. At the same time, performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and social influence do not affect behavioral intention, and behavioral intention significantly impacts use behavior. These results show that assisting users with information and solution services is crucial in banking.

articleTitle: Assessment of Potential Area for Solar Energy Investment in Northeastern Thailand by Entropy-TOPSIS Method
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the important engines of Thailand's food industrial growth however the cost of fossil energy is quite high for Thai farmers. Since Thailand has great solar potential, especially northeastern region, renewable energy sources of sunlight in this region should be considered to be another energy source for Thai agriculture. To assess and classify the potential of the investment in agricultural solar power systems of 20 provinces in Thailand's northeastern region, this study applied the combining method of Entropy Weight Method and TOPSIS with secondary data of solar irradiance, farmer household density, and income of farmer households. With this combining method, the results showed that farmer household density and income of farmer household were more influence on assessing and classifying the potential of this investment than solar irradiance. Finally, all 20 provinces were classified into four groups of Group A (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{12}}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{2}}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{4}}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{1}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{10}})$</tex>, Group B (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{8}}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{9}}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{19}}, \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{15}})$</tex>), Group C (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{17}},\ \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{13}},\ \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{18}} \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{16}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{20}}$</tex>) and Group D (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{6}},\ \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{11}},\ \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{7}},\ \mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{14}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}_{\mathbf{5}})$</tex> from the most potential province group for investment in agriculture solar power system to the least potential province group for investment in agriculture solar power system.

articleTitle: The Influence of Website Quality and Electronic Word of Mouth (e-WOM) on Hotel Rooms Booking Decisions in Online Travel Agents
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The rapid development of the internet today indicates a technological change that is increasingly advanced toward online-based media. Due to time constraints and perceived convenience, consumers search or surf the internet to get complete information about a product and service and make purchases online. The purpose of this research is to find out if website quality and e-WOM affect online room booking decisions through online travel agents in Indonesia. The research design seeks to test the hypotheses developed based on related theories. For finding and booking hotel accommodations, travelers are known to use the internet as their primary source of information. This study uses non- profitability and purposive sampling. The information required is obtained by distributing questionnaires using Google Forms online. A total of 208 people participated in this survey. The Smart PLS software was used for evaluating the data. The study's results found that website quality positively and significantly affected online booking intentions. There is a positive and significant effect of e-WOM on booking intention through online travel agents. There is a positive and significant effect between website quality and e-WOM.

articleTitle: Assessing the Effectiveness of Online Government Platform on Citizen Satisfaction in Promoting Civic Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research investigates the efficacy of the online government platform, focusing on M-Pajak, in promoting citizen satisfaction and fostering civic engagement. The study employs the IS Success Model and Technology Acceptance Model to assess factors such as information quality (IQ), system quality (SQ), customer satisfaction (CS), perceived usefulness (PU), and perceived effectiveness (PE). Through a comprehensive analysis of these dimensions, the research aims to provide insights into the platform's impact on citizen behavior and engagement with government services. By understanding the dynamics of citizen satisfaction and its connection to civic engagement, the research seeks to contribute valuable recommendations for optimizing digital governance initiatives. The findings are expected to enhance the understanding of how online government platforms, particularly M-Pajak, can effectively encourage citizen participation, elevate satisfaction levels, and contribute to the broader goals of transparent and efficient governance.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Elon Musk's Sentiment in Western and Indonesian News Outlets Headline: A Study Utilizing VADER Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to compare the portrayal of Elon Musk's sentiment in Western and Indonesian news outlets using a quantitative approach. Employing VADER sentiment analysis, this research investigates differences in news articles about Elon Musk, providing insights into varying media perceptions across distinct cultural and geographical contexts. The results highlight how media representation of prominent figures like Musk can significantly differ, reflecting the nuances of global media narratives and their potential impact on public perception and organizational decision-making.

articleTitle: Micro-Mobility in Indonesia: Examining the Legal and Policy Implications of Emerging Transportation Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study delves into micro-mobility in Indonesia, focusing on legal, safety, and policy aspects of electric scooters, bicycles, and similar devices. The absence of specific regulations and safety concerns pose challenges, compounded by infrastructure deficiencies and public perception complexities. A literature review provides insights, identifying gaps and guiding research goals. Legal analysis reveals a regulatory void, emphasizing the need for clear guidelines and dedicated safety measures, amid infrastructure challenges and public perception issues. The study underscores the importance of aligning urban planning, efficient enforcement, and public engagement for sustainable micro-mobility. A collaborative and comprehensive framework, incorporating clear regulations, safety measures, infrastructure development, efficient enforcement, and positive public perception, is essential for the successful integration of micro-mobility in Indonesia's urban landscape. Strategic and informed approaches are crucial as Indonesia leads the way in embracing these innovative transportation technologies.

articleTitle: Using Data Analytics to Enhance Co-Production
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: In the era of intense competition, businesses seek ways to survive and stay competitive. Data were used to leverage competitive advantage. Many manufacturers of consumer products have adopted the concept of co-production to improve their products and production processes, often utilizing big data. However, in the data-driven economy, businesses face the challenge of utilizing vast amounts of data from various sources to enhance manufacturing processes. This paper explores the relationship between data analytics, co-production, and management level. The findings indicate that businesses can benefit from utilizing DA to gain valuable insights into the impact of co-production. Furthermore, management level plays a role in moderating the extent of relationship between DA and co-production. This study is part of a larger ongoing research that covers additional aspects and provides deeper insight on the relationship between DA and co-production. Strategic implications are also discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Purchase Attractiveness of Online Fashion Buyers in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The study investigated factors influencing purchase attractiveness among university students. The independent factors were functional value, personal innovativeness, usefulness of online reviews, and fashion trends. The population of the research was university students at a large private university in Pathum Thani province, Thailand, with a sample of 318 survey questionnaires collected. Most respondents were females, around 20 years old, spending between 10,000 to 20,000 baht monthly. Most participants expressed interest in purchasing fashion items such as shirts, shoes, and pants online. The research employed descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis, revealing that only usefulness of online reviews and personal innovativeness had positive impact on purchase attractiveness, with a significance level of 0.01.

articleTitle: Design of Refrigerated Fish Container for Three Wheeler Electric Vehicle Using TRIZ Method
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Fish and fishery product (FFP) can be categorized as high perishable products that have specific requirements for storage and handling process. To ensure the quality of fish during distribution, the temperature of fish should be maintained in accordance with the requirement. Refrigerated container is designed to maintain the temperature of the fish during the distribution process. This study intends to design a refrigerated container to be mounted on a three-wheeler electric vehicle that was developed by Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember (ITS). This research uses the Theory of Resheniya Izobretatelskikh Zadatch (TRIZ) method which begins with in-depth interviews with fishmongers and refrigerated vehicle users and literature reviews. The next step is brainstorming with the refrigerated container product development team to determine the problem attributes. Technical responses were formed and the contradictions between the technical responses were analyzed using the TRIZ method. The result of this study is a design of a passively cooled refrigerated container for a three-wheeler electric vehicle using cold thermal energy storage (TES) system with a plate containing phase change material (PCM) to store cold energy. This refrigerated container uses polyurethane as the insulator which is covered by an aluminum plate.

articleTitle: User Experience for Online Course Strategies: EduFlex Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: User experience strategies are a critical component of UX design, involving multiple stakeholders to ensure the product team stays focused on solving the right problem and prioritises time and resources throughout the design process.
