In this paper, we review the theoretical features of educational online courses for Generation Alpha, delve into UI/UX design fundamentals, and assess standard AI tools used in the design process. A Three Hearts EduFlex Framework was developed as an agile UX approach crafted for online learning, emerging from this exploration. The framework encompasses foundational design elements informed by user research, addressing course discovery, enrollment, learning interfaces, and progress tracking. Essential components such as community-building pragmatism and personalised route map architecture underscore the significance of active designer attention to learners' qualities and desires. With hopes of speeding up design innovation, attention is directed to key UI design attributes catering to Generation Alpha. The paper concludes by advocating for a user-centred design approach, addressing the unique needs, behaviours, and expectations of Generation Alpha learners, contributing to the ongoing evolution of online education in the digital era.

articleTitle: Elucidating the Strategic Matter of Digital Resources Toward Work from Home Productivity in the Educational Institution
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: From a micro and macroeconomic perspective, work-from-home (WFH) productivity becomes a strategic matter. The purpose of this study is to elucidate how digital resources, such as the availability of digital support at home, and related working skills such as digital skills, digital cooperation, and digital leadership affect WFH productivity. A cross-sectional survey was carried out by Yayasan Pendidikan Telkom (YPT), an Indonesian higher education institution, with the participation of 2.082 academics, educational managers, and administrative staff. WFH novices make up the bulk of replies. The gathered data was assessed using SmartPLS version 3 as a variance-based structural equation modeling statistical tool. The result showed that WFH productivity was impacted by digital resources and technology support. Digital leadership of managers and/or supervisors doesn't directly affect them.

articleTitle: Object Detection for Retail Product Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The retail sector is a vital driver of economic growth. The retail industry must adopt technology to enhance productivity, streamline operations, and minimize human errors in order to continue its crucial economic role. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the purchasing power volumes globally grew from February 2020 to April 2021, and the retail sector gained 35 percents in market capitalization. This data highlights a compelling research opportunity. Consequently, artificial intelligence (AI) has become a focus of significant interest and has widely adopted technology, which includes computer vision to recognize and detect retail products. This paper aims to explore YOLO's performance in retail product recognition. The research compares different YOLO versions to identify on-shelf grocery items. In this research, YOLOv8 is applied and divided into five subcategories: YOLOv8n (nano), YOLOv8s (small), YOLOv8m (medium), YOLOv81 (large), and YOLOv8x (extra-large). They were evaluated with Grozi-120 and SKUII0K datasets. The evaluation metrics are precision, recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95. The result shows that YOLOv8x provides the best overall performance in both datasets, where mAP50 metrics exhibits the highest score at 92.6 percents in SKUII0K. The outcomes show that the YOLOv8 model works well for retail product detection.

articleTitle: Recommendation Systems in Education : A Bibliometric Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: In today's digital age, recommendation systems have become an important tool in many sectors, including education. This study presents a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of the literature related to recommendation systems in an educational context. Using major scientific databases and bibliometric analysis tools, we evaluate publications from the last 5 years to identify research trends, collaboration patterns, and methodological developments. Our results show a significant increase in the number of publications and interest in this field, with a wide variety of research themes ranging from personalized learning to optimization of educational resources. The most dominant analytics techniques include collaborative filtering and content-based filtering, while hybrid and deep learning approaches show growing potential. In addition, we identified geographic and institutional concentrations of research, as well as a set of challenges such as data privacy and the need for adaptation to learner dynamics. This research underscores the importance of recommendation systems in improving tailored educational experiences and supporting data-driven academic decisions. We also offer insights for future research directions, including the need for interdisciplinary research and closer international collaboration.

articleTitle: Predicting Customer's Intention to Use Drone Food Delivery in Jakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Currently, there is considerable interest in the utilization of drones in the food service sector, prompting numerous businesses to dedicate significant resources towards the development and implementation of drone-based food delivery services. However, our understanding of the customer attitudes towards the implementation of drone-based food delivery services, particularly in Indonesia, is still limited. Therefore, the objective of this study was to analyze the several factors that influence customers’ intentions to use drone-based food delivery services, specifically focusing on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and its components. Furthermore, the current study seeks to examine the influence of perceived innovativeness on customers' intentions to embrace drone-based food delivery services. Using a quantitative approach, the study involved the distribution of 176 questionnaires to the respondents. Data was analyzed using SmartPLS software. The results of the study revealed that perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness and perceived innovativeness significantly and positively influence customers’ attitude towards using drone food delivery services. In addition, the attitude significantly influenced the development of intentions to use drone food delivery services. The findings recommend that the business owner-manager in the food delivery industry should advocate for drones as a new and original food delivery method.

articleTitle: Technology Characteristics and User Perceptions on Behavioral Intention of Quick Response Code Indonesia Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Many countries have adopted the use of QRIS for payment transactions, but some users still adopt it even though payment with QRIS provides benefits and convenience for users. Therefore, this study analyzes the driving factors of user behavioral intention to adopt QRIS by paying attention to technological characteristics, task-technology fit, perceived ease of use, and perceived usefulness. The research population focused on QRIS users with a predetermined sample size of 383 QRIS users in three major cities in Indonesia (Surabaya, Sidoarjo, and Malang), so the purposive sampling method was applied in collecting data through social media. The data was then analyzed using the partial least square structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) method. The results prove that all hypotheses are accepted: technology characteristics affect task-technology fit. Task-technology fit affects perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness. Perceived ease of use affects perceived usefulness. Perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness affect behavioral intention in using QRIS.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Sustainable Highway Alignment Selection Using Automated Software: A Case Study in Myanmar
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research investigates how automated software can effectively evaluate highway alignments by incorporating sustainability. Trimble Quantm alignment planning software was selected for this study because it can quickly generate multiple alignments with associated cost and environmental data. A case study located within UTM Zone 47Q in Myanmar was used to illustrate the capability and efficiency of the software in comprehensive sustainable highway corridor selection. The findings showed that Quantm is an efficient supporting tool for highway alignment decision-making. However, some additional functionalities to support the sustainable planning framework are needed. The study suggests additional features and how to extend the Quantm planning software to enable sustainable highway alignment planning and analysis.

articleTitle: Digital Comfort: Decoding E-Service Excellence and E- WOM Influence on E-Satisfaction and Repeat Stays through OTA Platforms in Jakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: OT A apps connect travel service companies and consumers. Users can have good or bad OTA app experiences depending on numerous aspects. Online travel agencies (OTAs) do E-Service Quality differently. E-WOM may lead consumers to order from certain OTAs. This research examines how E-Service Quality and E-WOM affect Jakarta hotel reservations using OTA apps on E-Satisfaction and Repurchase Intention. Data processing sampled 238 Jakarta OTA users who have booked hotels many times. Questionnaires on Google Forms distribute data for analysis. For data analysis, questionnaires are distributed. Data study using SmartPLS 3 reveals that electronic service quality positively affects E-Satisfaction and repurchase intent. E- WOM also boosts E-Satisfaction and repurchase, according to studies. This study could help online travel agents (OTAs) position products to clients. To boost revenue, hotel businesses might focus on E-WOM.

articleTitle: The Effect of Digital Banking on E-Customer Satisfaction and E-Customer Loyalty
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study explores the dimensions of electronic service quality in digital banks, namely site organization, reliability, responsiveness, user-friendliness, personal needs, and efficiency. The research aims to analyze the effect of the dimensions of electronic service quality on electronic customer satisfaction and electronic customer loyalty with a case study of digital bank consumers in the Jakarta area. The research method used is associative descriptive research with a quantitative approach. The questionnaire in this study was carried out using a non-probability sampling method with a purposive sampling technique on 100 digital bank consumer respondents in Jakarta. Data analysis used Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) with SmartPLS, namely Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) using the Partial Least Squares (PLS) method. The results showed that the site organization and efficiency variables had a significant significantly affected satisfaction. The variables' reliability, responsiveness, user-friendliness, and personal needs do not exert a noteworthy impact on the satisfaction experienced by electronic customers. The variable pertaining to electronic customer satisfaction significantly influences the loyalty exhibited by consumers of digital banks in Jakarta. In summary, by means of the dimensions associated with service quality, digital banks will augment customer satisfaction and foster customer loyalty toward digital banking.

articleTitle: The Development of the Flexible Periodic Vehicle Routing Problem Model for Gas Cylinders Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Distribution plays a crucial role in business processes, and an efficient distribution system is necessary to minimize costs. Many companies, including those in the gas industry, are developing distribution models to reduce costs and maximize profits. Industrial gases are the main component of various sectors, such as the health industry, consumer goods, and more. Researchers have developed a model of Flexible Periodic Vehicle Routing Problem (FPVRP) for gas cylinder distribution, which considers profitability. The purpose of this model is to maximize profitability by considering storage costs, travel costs, and fixed costs. To achieve this, researchers have developed scheduling and routing methods by combining several models, such as the FPVRP, Inventory Routing Problem (IRP), Vehicle Routing Problem Simultaneous Delivery and Pickup (VRPSDP), and Vehicle Routing Problem with Profits (VRPPs). The model uses various models, such as the Visit Frequency Optimization Procedure (VFOP), which considers visit frequency and day combinations as decision variables, Nearest Neighbor, 2-opt Swap, and Taboo Search. The researchers have used Visual Basic Application (VBA) in Microsoft Excel to develop computerized models. The experiment results have shown that the proposed gas cylinder distribution model can provide maximum profit by reducing the costs of the entire system.

articleTitle: Exploring the Future of Hospitality: Will Jakarta's Hoteliers Embrace Service Robots?
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Due to a flourishing tourism sector and an increase of international guests, the hotel industry in Indonesia has experienced unprecedented expansion in recent years. The recent increase has given rise to obstacles and prospects for hotels in Jakarta. One noteworthy component of this development is the heightened focus on the incorporation of service robots. Although service robots are commonly used in the hospitality business in industrialized nations, their introduction in Indonesia, particularly in Jakarta, brings a distinct and ever-changing aspect to the field. This study aims to investigate the views of Generation Z which consist of hospitality students in Jakarta, who aspire to become hoteliers in the future, towards the prospective implementation of service robots in their professional duties. This research used a quantitative approach and convenient sampling techniques in collecting the data. There were 155 participants completed the questionnaire. This study identified a positive correlation between the performance of service robots and the willingness to implement them. In addition, it revealed that social influence, empathy, customer experience, service assurance, reliability, and communication and interaction all have a positive impact on the willingness to implement service robots. The expected results have the ability to provide precise insights customized to Jakarta's hotel industry, enabling strategic choices for the successful integration of service robots to enhance customer experience and operational effectiveness.

articleTitle: Sustainable Usage Intention: QRIS (Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard) Payment Acceptance for Small and Medium Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard (QRIS) has become a crucial development in the financial landscape of Indonesia, revolutionizing how transactions are carried out. The acceptance, ramifications, and wider consequences of QRIS in Indonesia are examined in this paper. This research aims to understand how widely QRIS has been adopted by the business world and consumers, and how it affects the dynamics of the country's economy. The main objective of the study was to use the UTAUT and TAM research methodologies to look at the sustainable use of QRIS payment. Micro, Small, and Medium-Sized Enterprises (MSME) represented the study population, while QRIS users made up the study sample. Samples was collected by random sampling via questionnaires, and SEMPLS was used for analysis. The results showed that there was no relationship between Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy and Consumer Trust with the Acceptance of QRIS Payment in Indonesia. In contrast, in Indonesia, consumer Acceptance of QRIS Payment was highly impacted by factors including Perceived Cost and Social Influence. Moreover, the Sustainable Usage Intention Variables were directly impacted by Acceptance of QRIS Payment in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Trajectory Optimization of Emergency Lane Change via Model Predictive Control Using a 1:10 Remote Control Car Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Autonomous vehicle technology holds the potential to significantly improve driving safety and precision, reducing the frequency and severity of road accidents. One of the fundamental features of this technology is the autonomous emergency lane change that enables a vehicle to evade unexpected obstacles rapidly. Accurate trajectory modeling and optimized path planning are crucial to performing this maneuver. This paper aims to evaluate the potential of the Model Predictive Control (MPC) model for vehicle stability control during emergency lane changes. A bicycle model was implemented to simulate the vehicle dynamics within a MATLAB Simulink, creating a closed-loop control system with an MPC controller. A 1:10 scale remote control car was used as the model vehicle. A quintic polynomial equation generated an initial trajectory and temporal yaw angles. Experimental conditions varied by initial longitudinal velocities from 0.5 m/s to 2 m/s, and the MPC model had a control horizon of 10 to 20% of a prediction horizon of 15. Our MPC model successfully generated vehicle trajectories for emergency lane change scenarios. At the longitudinal velocity of 0.5 m/s, the model car accurately followed the predicted trajectory. However, results at the longitudinal velocity of 2.0 m/s indicated divergence from the ideal trajectory, highlighting the impact of critical cornering speed on model performance. In addition, a higher number of control horizons yields a better-predicted trajectory that is close to the quintic polynomial function with a trade-off for limited stability. These findings demonstrate the potential of MPC controllers as optimizers for autonomous vehicles.

articleTitle: Eco-Revolution on Wheels: Understanding Hybrid Vehicle Uptake in Indonesia via Environmental Concerns and the Knowledge-Attitude-Behavior Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Vehicles with internal combustion engines are a major factor in urban air pollution. The production of hybrid vehicles has increased as a result of growing awareness of global warming and worries about potential future increases in gas and oil prices. The purpose of this study was to advance knowledge of the variables affecting consumers' intentions to adopt HV choices. This study proposes a behavioral model based on the construct of environmental concerns and customers' knowledge of HV concerning their influence on customer attitudes toward HV options and intention to adopt HV. Using information acquired from an online survey of 203 Indonesian car owners, the model was empirically tested using structural equation modeling analysis. The findings of this research indicated that environmental concerns and knowledge have a considerable impact on attitudes towards HV, and intention to adopt HV. The paper addresses the implications for the adoption of HV in Indonesia considers the findings and makes recommendations for further investigation. Based on this research, it is advised that governments and manufacturers work together to better utilize environmental concerns and HV knowledge strategies, in addition to concentrating on particular product attributes like performance and value for money in terms of energy consumption.

articleTitle: Understanding National Culture in Smart Technology Acceptance – A Case of Indonesia and Australia
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The attitude of employees is a crucial factor in the successful implementation of technological innovations in hotels. The influence of cultural values on an individual's conduct is highly significant. Previous studies have investigated the impact of national cultural values on technology acceptance, but primarily within the limits of a particular country. The purpose of current study is to assess the degree of technology acceptance in Indonesia and Australia through a comparative analysis of their national cultures, focusing on the contrasting cultural values of collectivism and individualism. This study used a quantitative methodology and a questionnaire survey to collect data. The study explicitly targets hotel employees, with 110 participants from Jakarta and 98 participants from Melbourne. In addition, this study employed SmartPLS 3.0 software and Multi-Group Analysis (MGA) to assess the gap in smart technology acceptability between both countries. The results indicated a direct relationship between the two nations with perceived usefulness and perceived ease of use. Furthermore, the present study emphasized the significance of employing smart technology aligns with the cultural norms of employees, especially in nations that embrace collective values. As the technology growth, these observations provide a foundation for adapting implementation strategies considering technological features and cultural differences.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Government Incentive Policy on Electric Motorcycle Purchase Intention in Indonesia: Content Analysis and PLS-SEM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The increasing use of electric vehicles in Indonesia has good hopes as the numbers continue to grow. It is hoped that the government's policy to provide incentives for electric motorcycle buyers will be a stimulant to increase sales and use of electric motorcycles. However, this incentive has not been maximized by the community so this incentive policy has not been fully absorbed. This research aims to explore the role of government incentives on purchasing electric motorcycles. The research method used is exploratory using a mixed method. First, using a qualitative method using content analysis from video comments on YouTube related to government incentives for electric motorcycles. Next, quantitative analysis was carried out using PLS-SEM to see the correlation of existing constructs. This research using 200 respondents from four major province in Indonesia. The research results show that there are four phases used in this research, viewing news before incentives, after incentives are implemented, changes to incentive policies, and changes to incentive conditions. The data shows the tendency of society to focus on policies and regulations for implementing incentives which are still difficult in the field. Incentives from the government have an influence on purchase intention of electric motorcycles.

articleTitle: Generalized Extreme Value Regression for Prediction of Meat Import Price Range in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Price range is one of the mechanisms that used to detect undervalued or overvalued prices for imported goods. The problem encountered in forming price range is that the data on the price of imported goods has an asymmetric distribution with non-stationary conditions or trends and covariates that change over time. GEV Regression model is a statistical analysis method used to model extreme value data with non-stationary conditions or the presence of trends and the influence of covariates that change over time. This research aims to apply the GEV Regression model to predict the import price range and obtain its significant predictor variables. Next, the ARDL model obtains the proper lag of the predictor variable within the GEV regression. The significant predictor for the maximum price of imported meat is the exchange rate one and two months earlier, along with the maximum price at three and four months earlier. Meanwhile, the significant predictor for the minimum price of imported meat is the exchange rate one month earlier and the minimum price one and two months earlier.

articleTitle: The Adoption of ICT in E-Business Development Among SMEs; the Case of Two Indonesian Tourism Villages
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research examines ICT adoption in developing MSME e-businesses in two Indonesian tourist villages. The research method used is pragmatism, which follows the technology acceptance model (TAM). The research data was obtained through Focus group discussions (FGD)s and questionnaires from two tourist villages in Indonesia namely Purwabakti Village and Pasanggrahan Village. This research showed that Purwabakti and Pasanggrahan villagers responded positively to their perception of use, perceived of usefulness, attitude towards use, experience towards use, social influence, and facilitating conditions of ICT adoption of e-business. However, villagers highly depend on the village government to develop e-businesses, while human resources constrain the governments of both villages.

articleTitle: An Evaluation on ICT Anxiety and Resilience of Phrada Bos Student and Improving Core Skill in Project Course
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The objectives of this paper were to develop the problem-based learning for improving using information technology, problem solving skill for Phrada Bos students. Starting from analysis, design, development, implement and evaluation of problem-based learning, identification of population and sample, implementation of problem-based learning for improving using information technology, problem solving skill for students that was designed, with Phrada Bos's students who study in PBL program, and then collect data, analysis and conclusion. The result found that anxiety was medium, and resilience was low, the post-test of using information technology skill was good level with average score 70.81 (S.D. = 2.97), problem solving skill was good level with average score 68.62 (S.D. = 4.16), the efficiency of problem-based learning in project course was 83.43/82.22 that were above 80/80 established criteria, the advanced abilities after learning of students who learned from problem-based learning in project course increased more than before learning, a knowledge and abilities of students were improved, the amount of the students learning achievement was 100% and almost project workpieces can meet industrial requirements.

articleTitle: Microplastic Spectral Classification Using Deep Learning with Denoising and Dimensionality Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Microplastic pollution poses a significant environmental threat, especially in marine ecosystems. It is necessary to have advanced techniques for accurate identification and classification. In this paper, we present two approaches to classifying microplastics from noisy Fourier transform in-frared spectra. The proposed approaches are constructed by combinations of an Autoencoder, a dimensionality-reduction method, and a deep-learning classification model. By using a dimensionality-reduction method, the proposed approaches achieve lower computational complexity than a traditional deep-learning classification model does while offering better or comparable classification performances. Experimental results show and compare the performances of the proposed approaches on six dimensionality-reduction methods and various levels of noise.

articleTitle: Intention to Use Netflix in Germany: A Modified Technology Acceptance Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The transformation of television consumption in the digital age, marked by the emergence of new media technologies, is particularly evident in the rise of over-the-top (OTT) streaming platforms. This study focuses on understanding the acceptance of Netflix among German consumers by adopting a modified version of the Technology Acceptance Model. The model includes key elements such as perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and attitude and introduces the external variable of facilitating conditions. While facilitating conditions were not found to affect perceived usefulness significantly, other relationships, including the influential role of attitude on intention to use, were supported. The study contributes to understanding the factors influencing the adoption of Netflix in Germany. It highlights the need for further research into the contextual dynamics influencing user behavior.

articleTitle: Enhancing Customer Satisfaction: A Comprehensive Analysis of Technological Innovations in Food Ordering, Serving, and Payment
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of technology on customer satisfaction in Asian restaurants, specifically focusing on food ordering, serving, and payment. Using a quantitative approach with a sample size of 240 respondents, collected data indicate that technology, as the main instrument in these restaurants, positively influences customer satisfaction. The study employed Google Forms with 24 questions on a five-point scale. The results show a mean score of four, indicating that food ordering, serving, and payment technologies contribute to increased customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: A Study on the Stacking Sequences of Laminated CFRP for the Design of Transfemoral Prosthetic Leg Socket
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The prosthetic leg socket is the frame protecting the residual limb and acts as a load-bearing component. Carbon fiber reinforced plastic (CFRP) is utilized as a prosthetic leg socket due to the high strength-to-weight ratio. The mechanical properties of CFRP depend on the fiber orientation and stacking sequences; therefore, it can be laminated to be able to withstand the weight of the patient. This study investigates the effect of fiber orientation and stacking sequences on the strength of CFRP transfemoral prosthetic leg socket using finite element analysis. The 3D model was constructed from 3D scan data of quadrilateral prosthetic leg socket donated from the patient whose weight is 100 kg. The proof force according to ISO10328:2016; standard for testing the structural prosthetic leg, was used as the criteria to evaluate the durability of socket with different fiber orientations. The results disclosed that the [45/-45] can withstand patient's weight with the maximum stress of 18.27 MPa, 120 g of socket weight and the 529.70 N maximum force at distal end of the socket, which was smaller than proof test force in ISO10328:2016. The results are helpful to the prosthetist to design the high durability but low weight CFRP prosthetic leg socket.

articleTitle: Bridging Gaps in Learning: Tracing the Trends of Differentiated Instruction in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study conducts a bibliometric analysis to explore Differentiated Instruction (DI) trends and evolution in higher education from 2000 to 2022. The research uses Scopus academic databases to analyse publication and citation trends, co-citation networks, and keyword occurrences to offer a comprehensive view of DI's development in tertiary education. Key findings indicate a significant increase in DI-related publications and citations, reflecting growing interest and research in this area. The analysis reveals a shift from theoretical discussions to practical applications, emphasizing technology's role in DI. The study highlights the geographical distribution of DI research, uncovering global patterns and regional contributions. It also points out gaps, particularly in empirical studies and interdisciplinary approaches. This research is a valuable resource for educators, policymakers, and researchers. It underscores DI's potential in addressing diverse learning needs and suggests directions for future research.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Review of End-of-Life Management of Electric Vehicle Batteries in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Thailand is rapidly emerging as a significant player in the electric vehicle (EV) manufacturing industry. It possesses the potential to become a major center for managing EV batteries (EVBs). Thailand is well-positioned to lead in the responsible disposal, remanufacturing, repurposing, and recycling of EVBs. This potential stems from the country's capacity to innovate cutting-edge technologies, supported by a commitment to environmental sustainability through policy initiatives and growing public awareness. By analyzing the current landscape, existing policies, technological innovations, and inherent challenges, Thailand can develop a circular economy model for EVBs, contributing significantly to global environmental objectives while positioning itself as a leader in responsible EVB management on the international stage.

articleTitle: Immersive Learning in Using the Metaverse of Satellite Communication Systems Science
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Education stands out as one of the most impactful applications of the metaverse, holding immense potential for the future. Within the realm of satellite communication system science education, the integration of immersive learning through the metaverse adds a layer of interest and interactivity to the teaching and learning process. Numerous design and evaluation techniques have been employed in a growing body of research, aiming to understand how immersive learning via the metaverse can effectively contribute to specific educational objectives. Hence, this research is dedicated to delving into the development of an immersive learning metaverse model for the science of satellite communication systems. The research contributes a model that advocates for a holistic learning approach by integrating metaverse technology, VR, the 6E Instructional Process Model, and the MSLQ evaluation instrument. The objective of this model is to enhance the efficiency, effectiveness, and interactivity of learning within the field of satellite communication systems science.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence Influencers on Purchase Intention
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research aims to examine the influence of trustworthiness, attractiveness, and parasocial relationships on artificial intelligence influencers. Meanwhile, another objective of this study is to determine the influence of artificial intelligence influencers on purchase intentions. The research is classified as quantitative research using SmartPLS 3 software as a statistical tool. The sample in this research was 100 respondents using a purposive sampling technique. The results of this research show trustworthiness, attractiveness, and parasocial relationships influence perceived AI influencer-customer product fit. Another conclusion from this research is that perceived AI influencer-customer product fit influences purchase intention. The practical implication of research conducted on companies is that AI influencers can be an effective and efficient promotional strategy that can increase purchase intention. In addition, using AI Influencers can create unique potential consumer experiences, so that they match preferences, create more interesting interactions, and build stronger engagement.

articleTitle: Moolang: Cultural Internalization Through Interactive Learning Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Gamification is the utilization of game design elements in non-game environments. This research introduces the Moolang Platform, a suitable platform that contains interactive game-based media platforms. Various features are developed on this platform, including avatar selection with Indonesian cultural costumes, a whiteboard and seating arrangement resembling a classroom, a library feature, chat functionality between teachers and students, a raise hand feature for students, and a group discussion feature. The main objectives of this research are (1) To design and create a game-based learning platform with cultural internalization as a learning medium for students with the hope that this research is applicable and easy for educators and readers to understand, (2) To be able to increase student interest in learning economics with a gamification learning approach, (3) To form students with character who understand economics and knowledge of Indonesian culture. Answering the paper's aim, this study analyzed using the qualitative approach utilizing the Design-Based Research (DBR) methodology. The finding is the application limitation lies in the absence of visual communication features between teachers and students. Therefore, future research endeavors are encouraged to address this deficiency.

articleTitle: Comparative Online Learning Challenges of Students in Selected Private and Public Schools in South Manila Educational Consortium (SMEC)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Online distance learning proved its worth during the COVID-19 pandemic. Challenges among students in the private and public schools surfaced which served as bases for designing a proposed Consortium Online Learning Hub for Tertiary Students. The study employed a mixed-method research design specifically the explanatory sequential design to compare the students' online learning challenges of selected private and public schools in the South Manila Educational Consortium (SMEC). A survey questionnaire, a combination of quantitative and qualitative open-ended questions that is expert-validated with high reliability was administered to tertiary students in the consortium. The findings revealed that students in the private and public schools were moderately challenged in terms of attitudes toward online learning and fairly challenged by the online learning modality. Significant differences existed between the challenges of students in private and public schools along network connections, support from the school, online education implementation/training, proper online behavior, school-life balance, and distance education modalities.

articleTitle: The Artificial Intelligence, Robots and Employee Well-Being: An In-Depth Analysis of Job Stress and Job Satisfaction in the Restaurant Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study explores the interplay between Artificial Intelligence (AI), robots, and human psychology in the restaurant industry. It investigates how these factors influence job stress and job satisfaction among restaurant employees. A quantitative approach was employed, with data collected through questionnaires distributed to 210 employees in DKI Jakarta. The study found that the perceived usefulness and ease of use of AI and robots positively impact employee attitudes toward these technologies. However, contrary to the initial hypothesis, a positive attitude towards technology was not directly linked to increased job stress. These findings suggest that prioritizing the perceived usefulness and ease of use of AI and robots during integration can lead to positive employee attitudes and potentially reduce stress. The study highlights the importance of addressing potential stressors, ensuring user-friendly integration, and considering ethical implications for successful AI and robot integration in the restaurant industry.

articleTitle: Exploring Entrepreneurial Students’ Attitudes Towards Integrating Creativity-Based Learning and Critical Language Skills
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The research examines entrepreneurial students’ attitudes toward integrating creativity-based learning and critical language skills at a large private university's language institute. 109 participants from the School of Entrepreneurship and Management were studied, revealing diverse demographics: 58.72% female, 34.86% male, and 6.42% identifying otherwise, with most in Year 1 (93.58%). Results showed participants generally agreed on the efficacy of creativity-based learning, indicating its benefits in problem-solving (mean = 4.070), innovation (mean = 3.901), enjoyment (mean = 4.098), critical thinking (mean = 3.696), and future career prospects (mean = 4.446). They also recognized its positive impact on critical language skills (mean = 4.098) and language proficiency (mean = 3.839), highlighting its effectiveness in enhancing language skills. Feedback highlighted benefits like improved speaking, problem-solving, creativity, and language development, alongside challenges such as confidence issues and vocabulary limitations. Recommendations included more activities, emphasizing everyday vocabulary use, and promoting a continuous learning mindset. Qualitative insights from interviews delved deeper, emphasizing positive perceptions of creativity-based learning's impact on problem-solving and language skills, while noting implementation challenges like time constraints and resistance from traditional structures. Themes of real-world applicability, varied learning preferences, and fostering an entrepreneurial mindset emerged, enriching understanding.

articleTitle: Predicting the Determinants of Artificial Intelligence in Green Energy Technologies Adoption Intention at the Household Level Using Structural Equation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Sustainability is a present concern in many developing countries, where the role of the household is pivotal in realizing its benefits. This study aims to explore artificial intelligence in green energy technologies (AIGET) adoption intention among household-level respondents selected in the National Capital Region (NCR), Philippines. The study has 446 respondents and analyzed using partial least squares and structural equation modeling approaches (PLS-SEM). Among the factors tested, results revealed that perceived usefulness is the strongest predictor of AIGET adoption intention. Factors such as usefulness, ease of use, subjective norms, and perceived risk have a positive effect on attitude. This confirms that attitude has a positive impact on behavioral intention on AIGET. Finally, this study shows that household-level participants have a positive interest in adopting AIGET, considering its usefulness and ease of use. This study presents useful theoretical and practical contributions to further its uptake in the Philippines and other developing countries.

articleTitle: Species Classification and Counter for Mixed-Species Bird Flock Using ResNet9 Network and YOLOv5 Object Detection Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Bird's population is essential to ecology and conservation initiatives. However, proper categorization and counting in mixed-species flocks presents significant challenges because of the complexity due to increasing number of different species with diverse looks. Deep learning and computer vision techniques are used to automate the procedure to overcome these obstacles. This paper discusses the method to develop a graphic analyzing system for detection, classifying of bird species and counting, leveraging the ResNet9 network and YOLOv5 algorithm. Convolutional neural network (CNN) is also utilized for image classification process wherein a pre trained architectures named ResNet9 to identify the bird species. It improves its network feature extraction ability by overcoming the vanishing gradient as it skips the convolutional layer and can stack hundreds of layers. The models were trained using images collected from eBird.org. Pre-processing of the ResNet9 model involves oversampling and image augmentation techniques to handle imbalanced data. A recall of 97.67% for the YOLOv5 and 98.12% and 95.34% for the validation and testing of ResNet9, show how well the network and algorithm are applied to accurately classify bird species and provide counts of the bird species within flocks. With this, the study will be useful in a bird monitoring environment.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Hotel Website Quality E-Service on Customer E-Satisfaction, E-Trust, and Online Repurchase Intention in Jakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The utilization of sophisticated technology in the hotel industry, such as thoughtful and efficient hotel websites, significantly contributes to delivering a seamless and pleasurable customer experience. It could also impact on the confidence of potential guests when making booking decisions. The lack of quality hotel websites resulted in decreased and stagnant hotel sales. This study aims to measure customer's trust and satisfaction when using a hotel's website for purchasing and measure the possibility of potential customers repurchasing the hotel product through the website. This research used a quantitative approach with a correlation research type. An online survey questionnaire was distributed to 200 respondents as research samples to collect the data for this study, using a convenient sample method. The data was analyzed using the third version of Smart PLS. The result of the study found that there were positive and significant relationships between the variables. The findings of this research are expected to recommend to the hotel industry that improving the quality of hotel websites could increase sales and trust, reach customer satisfaction, and lead customers to make repurchases on the website.

articleTitle: How Social Accountability and Internet Usage May Contribute to Human Capital Development: A Case from Selected Asian Economies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: To understand how the internet affects human capital development in Asia, this research tries to understand the complex relationship between the digital environment and the fundamental principles of social accountability and the voice of the people. The intricacies that impact millions’ quality of life in this diverse and vibrant continent are this study interdisciplinary focus. Through understanding these relationships, the study is expected to contribute to the discussion on the internet's transformative power in promoting equitable and inclusive human development in Asia. Social accountability and governance focus on the principles of voice and accountability of the society (freedom of speech, freedom of association, and free media), and how they affect the overall quality of human development in Asia. The findings indicate at least two main things: (1) Internet usage promotes better human capital quality, while (2) Voice and accountability impair the human capital development index if there are poor governance, economic challenges, and instability in government-public institutions. These findings applied to the studied timeframe on 14 selected economies, therefore, further studies are needed to provide a more general and global implications.

articleTitle: Detection and Tracking Shape-Shifting Gold Necklaces Using Computer Vision Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Due to the current method of theft in gold shops, criminals were stealing gold necklaces or gold jewelry. They were concealing it, which employees did not know that gold had disappeared from the gold shop. The shopkeeper found it difficult to track directly from the object and physical gold necklaces were small for easy stacking. This research focuses on a study and analysis of the detection and tracking of deformable gold necklaces. Therefore, it was observed in many follow-up experiments. After that, the researcher presented the detection and tracking of deformable gold necklaces had been using image processing techniques. The researcher will improve the gold necklace tracking performance with the traditional Gaussian mixture model (GMM) enhanced with the adaptive background subtraction (ABS) functionality. We compared the traditional GMM method and the optimized GMM with an adaptive background subtraction (ABS) image. The results of the experiment were shown in the method to compare efficiency before and after improving efficiency. It was found that 86.07% of the frames could be tracked properly.

articleTitle: Bivariate Poisson Inverse Gamma INAR(1) Regression Model: Healthcare Service Visits by Health Insurance Members Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The integer-valued Autoregressive (INAR) model is a statistical approach for modeling positive integer time series data. There are two components in the INAR model: the correlation structure, which utilizes a binomial thinning operator, and the marginal distribution, which is mixed Poisson. Accommodating strict assumptions in Poisson, Inverse gamma is chosen as the associated mixing distribution because of its good performance in accommodating overdispersion data with heavy tails. The Bivariate Poisson Inverse Gamma INAR (1), BPIGA-INAR(1), is proposed to model and analyze a positive integer time series data set from Badan Penyelenggara Jaminan Sosial (BPJS) in Indonesia. The data set provides information about the total number of healthcare service visits by health insurance members diagnosed with diabetes and heart disease from 2015 to 2020. The parameter estimation process is conducted using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and Genetic Algorithms (GA), while the Maximum Likelihood Ratio Test (MLRT) is used for hypothesis testing. BPIGA-INAR(1) model was established as a suitable model for the data set, with age and gender have significant impacts on the number of healthcare service visits by each health insurance member diagnosed with diabetes disease and the inclusion of an ‘unemployed’ category in the Membership segment for heart disease.

articleTitle: Unleashing Electronic Word of Mouth (eWOM): How Positive Online Buzz Shapes Your Buying Choices
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to identify the effect of the Electronic Positive Word of Mouth (ePWOM) on perceived value, trust beliefs, and information quality. Besides, it is to examine the effect of perceived value, trust beliefs, and information quality on purchase intention in Paxel Market services and to initiate strategies to increase consumer interest in using Paxel Market services. This study used a quantitative approach and data were collected by distributing questionnaires online. The determination of the sample used a purposive sampling technique with a total of 100 respondents. Data were analyzed using SmartPLS. The results showed that E-PWOM affected trust belief, perceived value, and information quality. Information quality affected purchase intention. This study has some implications such as the business strategy of Paxel Market to improve ePWOM by increasing customer reviews regarding service quality and information quality shared on various company social media in order to increase consumer purchase intention at Paxel Market.

articleTitle: Improving Term Weight with Normalized Class Mutual Information for Sentiment Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The relevance of keywords in a document is assessed by assigning a higher term weight to them. The conventional use of Tf and Idf in short documents may introduce biases. Various term weighting strategies have been proposed to enhance the meaning of term weights by addressing each component individually, aiming for a more nuanced and refined representation. This study enhances the efficiency of Tf-Idf term weighting for sentiment classification by incorporating Normalized Class Mutual Information (NCMI). In our proposed method, the NCMI value is computed to assess the discriminative power of each term in distinguishing between positive and negative classes. The experiment utilizes three datasets, Amazon, IMDB, Magazine, Books, DVD, Electronics, and Kitchen_housewares, along with two sentiment classifications, NB and Random forest. The results demonstrate that the NCMI can improve the classification accuracy and F1-measure.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network (ANN) Modeling to Forecast the Solar Radiation on Vertical Planes in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This paper presents an artificial neural network (ANN) modeling of forecasting one-hour ahead solar radiation on vertical planes oriented north, east, south, and west. A set of records from a meteorological station in Bangkok Thailand during the year 2019–2022 was used for the modeling. By analyzing the parameter correlation, the normalized global solar radiation index, ambient air temperature, solar elevation, and beam incidence angle on vertical plane were selected to be the model input-features. Evaluation results showed that the models were able to forecast the total vertical radiation on north, east, south, and west facing planes with normalized mean bias error (nMBE) of 1.1%, 0.3%, 4.5%, and 3.5%, and the normalized root mean square error (nRMSE) of 18.0%, 22.0%, 15.3%, and 18.5%, respectively. The proposed ANN models outperformed the existing ANN models that needed coupling with a transposition model to convert its forecasted horizontal radiation to the vertical solar radiation.

articleTitle: ESD-EDU Simulator: Game Based Learning Strategy to Foster Student Motivation in Entrepreneurship
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: From a macro perspective, entrepreneurship is one of the contributors to economic growth in a country. So, the state encourages increasing the quality and quantity of entrepreneurship in Indonesia. Universities have an important role in creating new entrepreneurs. So, learning in higher education should prepare students to have entrepreneurial skills. This research aims to analyze the implementation of simulation-based learning, namely the ESD-EDU Simulator, to increase students' motivation to develop their business plans. What is meant by ESD-EDU Simulator is a game that we developed ourselves as a business simulation tool in Entrepreneurship classes. This research uses a classroom action research method with two cycles. The research results show that simulation-based learning can increase students' motivation to become entrepreneurs.

articleTitle: User Experience Evaluation on Mobile Banking Application at PT Bank Nagari
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to evaluate the user experience (UX) in the mobile banking application of PT Bank Nagari and identify the suitability of features in the application with user needs. The method used is the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ), which is a comprehensive measurement of user experience. A quantitative approach was employed using the UEQ as the data collection instrument. The data were analyzed using the UEQ tool, and the research findings indicated the level of user satisfaction with the PT Bank Nagari mobile banking application across the dimensions of attractiveness (1.77), perspicuity (2.13), efficiency (1.75), dependability (2.08), stimulation (1.92), and novelty (1.44). Evaluation was also conducted on the app's interface and features in line with user needs. This research contributes to improving the quality of banking services and assists PT Bank Nagari in meeting the evolving needs of users by creating design mockups based on the analysis results. The findings can serve as a foundation for further product development. This research provides a better understanding of user experience in mobile banking applications and helps PT Bank Nagari address challenges in app development.

articleTitle: Exploring the School Innovation Ecosystem in Nurturing Student Innovators of Tomorrow
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study investigates the key elements of the innovation ecosystem in schools that aim to foster future student innovators. A concept sampling strategy in the form of purposive sampling was used to recruit seventeen participants from various sectors. The semi-structured interview technique was employed for data collection, while open, axial, and selective coding methods were applied for data analysis. Based on the conceptual definition framework for the innovation ecosystem, which has three main components (actors, activities, and artifacts), the results identified the actors as school administration, teachers/facilitators, parents, external experts, external partnerships, and government. The activities encompassed school management, curriculum design, and instructional management. The artifacts included knowledge, learning resources, technologies and platforms, research, and intellectual property. The implications of this study are discussed.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis on Blockchain Perception in Higher Education in the Philippines and Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The researchers investigated the level of familiarity of respondents with blockchain technology in the context of higher education. Specifically, the study examined how respondents in the Philippines and Thailand perceived the competitive advantage of prioritizing blockchain integration in higher education. The researchers tested the significant correlation between respondents' awareness of blockchain and their perceived competitive advantage of the technology in both countries. The results indicated that Filipinos were more familiar with blockchain in higher education Ihan Thais, likely because Philippine schools offer it as an elective course. Filipinos also viewed blockchain as a more relevant and advantageous technology than Thais, who perceived it as moderately relevant. Notably, the null hypothesis was rejected in the Philippines, indicating a significant relationship between respondents’ awareness of blockchain and their perceived competitive advantage of the technology, while the null hypothesis was accepted in Thailand. The study suggests that higher educational institutions should consider adopting blockchain för credentialing due to its ease of use, cost­ effectiveness, robust features, and secure record-keeping capabilities. Additionally, Thailand should prioritize raising public awareness of blockchain technology by hiring experts to educate people about its potential benefits.

articleTitle: Exploring the Relationship Between Passion, Satisfaction, and Academic Efficacy in High School Constructionism
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Constructionist learning is an educational approach that emphasizes the active role of students in creating their own knowledge and understanding. However, little is known about how this approach affects the students' academic functioning, which includes their engagement, motivation, satisfaction, and achievement. This paper explores how passion, school satisfaction, and academic efficacy are related among high school students who learn in a constructionist environment. The study involved 94 high school students from a school that adopted constructionist learning principles, selected using a purposeful sampling method. The Pearson r correlation test results revealed that passion was positively related to both school satisfaction and academic efficacy, and academic efficacy was positively related to school satisfaction. These findings suggest that constructionist learning can foster students' passion for learning, which in turn can enhance their satisfaction and efficacy in school. This paper contributes to the constructionist theory by providing empirical evidence for the benefits of this approach. It also offers practical implications for constructionist educators who want to improve their professional learning and adopt effective strategies for their contexts and learning goals.

articleTitle: Analysis of Essential Factors that Influence the Youth Generation to Invest in FinTech
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: FinTech startups in Indonesia have been around for a while and have recently spread to several financial areas. It has been discovered that 32% of millennials and 13% Generation Z Americans likely to use FinTech investment services on a large scale in the future and Africa's financial startup industry is expected to grow at a 10% yearly rate by 2025. However, this phenomenon is not found in Indonesia, hence this is the research basis for this study. Several prior studies identified crucial elements influencing FinTech investing services. In addition to previous research, this study identifies eight factors: E-Trust, Financial Literacy, Social Influence, Personal Interest, Environment, Hedonism, Service Quality, and Actual Use of FinTech. From these elements, a novel research model will be developed and employed in this study. The data comprises 468 Indonesian youth respondents which used the FinTech investment. This study employed a qualitative approach and PLS-SEM as the research method, with snowball sampling for data collecting and SmartPLS as the statistical tool. The findings revealed that the personal interest variable had a 49.4% impact on service quality which lead 73.5% on intention to employ FinTech investment. However, this study discovered that the independent variables employed, all had a significant impact on service quality (89.6%) and hedonism (89.9%). This demonstrates that independent variables have a significant impact on service quality and hedonism, which influences the younger generation's inclination to use FinTech investment. However, there are certain critical independent features, such as E-Trust, which requires application enhancement, and financial literacy, which necessitates increased awareness on both the part of the FinTech investment provider and the user. These findings are very useful for supporting the development of the FinTech application industry.

articleTitle: An Exploratory Study on Key Factors Influencing Thai Student Attitudes Towards Onsite Learning (Part I)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to examine factors influencing student attitudes towards onsite learning at the university level. This research employed quantitative method where discrete and continuous probabilities were used for hypothesis testing. The proposed model consisted of 6 independent variables, namely personal experience (x1), culture (x2), influence of others environment (x3), media motivation (x4), educational institutions and religion (x5) and student's emotional factors (x6). The data for this research came from 119 surveys of undergraduate students from 9 majors all studying in the Thai program at a private university in Thailand. A 95 percent confidence interval was utilized and each variable was tested in simple regression and all were found statistically significant. However, when combined, empirical testing shows that only experience, media and culture are statistically significant. Each variable shows R square of 0.25, 0.25 and 0.30, respectively. The interactions among the three variables shows statistical significance for all pairs: x1x2, x1x3 and x2x3 with pValue < 0.05. The outcomes also show that educational institutions and religions, emotions and environment do not impact student's attitudes towards onsite learning. The paper also recommends policy guidelines to better comprehend Thai student's attitudes towards onsite learning at the university level.

articleTitle: Motivation for Japanese Language Learning Among Students at Thai-Nichi Institute of Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This paper investigates the motivation for Japanese language learning of students at Thai- Nichi Institute of Technology (TNI), a university that emphasizes Japanese cultural aspects as part of its higher education mission. The research used a questionnaire adapted from previous research to measure the motivation of 968 students from three faculties who were studying Japanese as a compulsory subject. The research divides the students into top and bottom groups based on their grades and compares their motivation levels using descriptive statistics and t-tests. The paper identifies four groups of items related to different aspects of motivation, such as entertainment, culture, knowledge, curiosity, work, and influence from others. The research findings indicate that the top group has significantly higher motivation than the bottom group in most items, except for those related to entertainment and culture, which show ceiling effects in both groups. The paper suggests that the top group corresponds to the “Integration Regulation” stage of the Organismic Integration Theory, where students internalize their motivation for Japanese language learning. The paper also discusses the limitations of the questionnaire and the need for a new scale to measure motivation in the context of the Japanese cultural boom in Thailand.

articleTitle: Student Engagement in Open Distance Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Creating an immersive virtual environment in open distance learning is essential to enhance student engagement. Therefore, this study aims to predict the factors that drive student engagement in universities that run open distance learning: ease of use of learning management system (LMS), experience quality, service value, and relevant information. This research uses quantitative techniques with primary data sources from students’ responses in five study programs at BINUS Online. Of the 336 students, they responded to the questionnaire distributed via email with a simple random sampling technique. PLS-SEM was used to answer the research hypothesis. The findings of this study revealed that ease of use of the LMS and relevant information positively and significantly influenced the quality of experience and perceived service value. In addition, it was also found that the four endogenous variables had a positive and significant effect on student engagement behavior. Furthermore, this study contributes to universities that run open distance learning to encourage and enhance student engagement to achieve sustainability and recognition of the open distance learning market.

articleTitle: Transforming Board Exam Readiness for Future Engineers Through Digitalization and Comprehensive Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: With the shifting landscape of education, traditional review centers need to be reevaluated, leading to the integration of digital platforms and Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC). This research addresses the challenges arising from this transformation, focusing on effective technology utilization, secure online assessments, and maintaining educational standards. Additionally, financial support alternatives are discussed, emphasizing the importance of affordability and inclusiveness concerns. This study examines the Innovative Engineering Board Examination Website System comprehensively, taking into account study session styles, materials availability, cost, and flexibility. Through insight into these factors, the research facilitates flexible, accessible engineering learning by fostering online review centers. In addition to improving engineering licensing test preparation, it may also enhance educational paths. With engineering education constantly evolving, this study envisions a technological leap in review centers at the College of Engineering that will revolutionize the industry. This study examines external factors, individual personalities, and marketing strategies that align services with board examiner preferences in order to determine the ideal review center criteria. Based on these findings, new marketable, convenient, and cost-effective review centers will be able to be created, reflecting the need for adaptability in an ever-changing field such as engineering licensure exam preparation.

articleTitle: Analysis of Thai Government Projects Using Geographic Distribution from Electronic Monitoring and Evaluation System of National Strategy and Country Reform (eMENSCR)
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This work investigates the geographical distribution of Thai government projects using straightforward choropleth (color-coded region) and pin (marked point) maps. Our aim is to develop a robust tool with easy-to-understand visuals and extract practical insights for decision-making. First, we import a dataset from Electronic Monitoring and Evaluation System of National Strategy and Country Reform (eMENSCR) to MongoDB and design the data pipeline to select the fields and subfields. Second, the Province Code, Amphur Code, and Tambon Code are filled and mapped into the new collection. Then, APIs for each map layers are created to show the Choropleth map on Leaflet with four layers. We anticipate producing clear maps, analyzing data, and providing actionable recommendations to optimize government project allocation strategies for improved planning, efficiency and analyze in six different aspects.

articleTitle: Implementation of Single Shot Multibox Detector (SSD) Algorithm for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study presents an innovative implementation of the Single Shot Multibox Detector (SSD) algorithm for real-time object detection on the Raspberry Pi 4. It harnesses the synergies of Python programming, the OpenCV computer vision library, and the SSD algorithm's adaptability. Python, chosen for its versatility, is the programming language, while OpenCV forms the backbone for implementing the finely tuned SSD algorithm. The resulting modular script, designed for real-time object detection, incorporates optimization techniques such as frame skipping and region of interest cropping to enhance Raspberry Pi 4 performance. The system demonstrates promising results, showcasing accurate and responsive object detection in resource-constrained environments. The Raspberry Pi 4's versatility makes it the solution for diverse edge computing applications, including surveillance, robotics, and intelligent environments. Computational constraints prompted the adoption of optimizations, while identified challenges illuminate future research directions exploring advanced algorithms and considering more potent hardware variants. This study contributes significantly to the intersection of computer vision and edge computing, underscoring the successful implementation of the SSD algorithm on the Raspberry Pi 4 and encapsulating technical achievements, practical implications, and a roadmap for future advancements in real-time object detection.

articleTitle: User Experience and Barriers in Telemedicine Virtual Healthcare Service Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The use of telemedicine and virtual healthcare services has gained much attention, especially during the digital transformation of countries. This study aims to explore the experience of users and the barriers they face when using telemedicine virtual healthcare service platforms. Scientific studies were reviewed to identify the barriers, facilitators, user attitudes, and telemedicine implementation experiences. The results of prior studies suggest that the primary impediment to adopting telemedicine services is the lack of familiarity with virtual software platforms. Significant barriers were identified, such as inadequate information communication technology infrastructure, cultural resistance to using technology in healthcare delivery, and financial obstacles. Furthermore, the study examined the perspectives of healthcare providers and patients, highlighting their concerns and expectations regarding the use of telemedicine. The analysis also delved into the effects of telemedicine on healthcare utilization, patient satisfaction, and the potential role of virtual reality in rehabilitation. The study provides insights into the challenges and opportunities of integrating telemedicine into healthcare systems. It also offers recommendations for addressing the obstacles and enhancing the user experience in telemedicine virtual healthcare service platforms. The ultimate goal of this study is to improve patient outcomes and strengthen healthcare accessibility through optimized user experiences.

articleTitle: Psychological Impact of Using the Sileb Information System As An Smart Learning Platform In Senior High School
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The aim of this research is to look at the psychological impact of using smart learning applications in high school. Sileb is proven to improve the quality of learning to be better and more efficient, especially in the regions. Sileb is a more effective and efficient learning method and can replace teachers' duties in delivering learning material, giving assignments and practice questions, as well as helping students learn to become more independent individually wherever and whenever. Sileb is equipped with online attendance and exam facilities. Silep development was carried out by applying agile development and the SCRUM Framework to produce a learning system that suits user needs. The evaluation was carried out using the quantitative linear regression method in system testing and then compared with in-depth discussions with learning psychology experts. The results of this research prove that Sileb has a positive impact because there is an increase in students' interest in learning. Likewise with teachers who like to improvise with their teaching models. This research can still be developed by using a wider range of users or different versions so that it can further influence the evaluation of the use of the Intelligent Learning Information System.

articleTitle: Development of Microservices Software to Connect Communications between Services
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study objective is to develop a microservice that can bridge communication between services at PT Soluix. This company has a microservice application that has problems in managing the communication flow between its services. They apply a direct communication method from one service to another which makes each service must change every time there is a need to define communication with other services, this makes the communication flow non-uniform and increasingly complicated to manage as services increase. To make the uniformity of communication flow management, an orchestrator is needed that becomes the center of communication so that there is no need to define communication flow in each service. The result achieved is a microservice that becomes the center of communication flow management. The research method starts with problem identification, data collection, system design, implementation, and then evaluation. The conclusion obtained is that the communication orchestrator between microservice services can help manage the communication flow between services to be uniform and not affected by the number of services in a microservices ecosystem.

articleTitle: A Study of Instructional Needs on Japanese Language for Working Individuals
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The purposes of this research were 1) to study the instructional needs of Japanese language for working individuals in seven aspects: Contents, Teaching Materials, Japanese Language Skills, Teaching-Learning Process, Teaching Activities, Teaching Approach and Instructor and 2) to gather supplemental suggestions from learners and instructors. Research samples were 46 Thai-Nichi Institute of Technology students in the first semester of the 2023 academic year, derived through a simple random sampling technique. The instruments used for gathering the data were the rating-scale and open-ended questionnaire. The statistics used for analyzing the data were frequency, percentage, mean and standard deviation. The results showed that instructional needs on Japanese for working individuals as a whole were at a high level (mean <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 4.31, SD <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$=$</tex> 0.09).
