Instructors provided supplemental suggestions, emphasizing the need to adapt teaching methods and enhance their skills when developing Japanese language courses for working individuals, considering the situation and suitability for the learners.

articleTitle: Reflection Support Function in a Metaverse-Based Evacuation Training System
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Disaster preparedness is crucial, and evacuation training plays a vital role in it. Recently, the metaverse, which is social virtual reality, has been expanding. A prototype of an evacuation training system based on the metaverse has been developed, offering a three-dimensional virtual world. In this system, an earthquake strikes suddenly, prompting users to seek safe places for evacuation. These users can be regarded as participants in the evacuation training. A reflection support function is being implemented that will allow participants to review their evacuation behaviors by replaying them in both first- and third-person views. A preliminary comparative experiment revealed that this function can support reflection regardless of the first- or third-person view.

articleTitle: Cross-Cultural Perspectives on Netflix Adoption: A Comparative Analysis Between Indonesia and Germany Using a Modified Technology Acceptance Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: A growing number of people are using Over the Top (OTT) technology for streaming TV shows and movies, with Netflix leading as a prominent OTT television provider boasting over 247 million global subscribers. This study utilizes a Modified Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) to investigate Netflix adoption in Indonesia and Germany. The research compares user intentions and evaluates the modified TAM's efficacy in a cross-cultural context, addressing existing research gaps. Online questionnaires were distributed to 150 respondents in each country, and the modified model was analyzed using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). Results show the proposed TAM-based scale effectively explained factors related to Netflix use among Indonesian and German users. Findings provide valuable insights for strategic decisions in the global expansion of streaming platforms and inform policymakers, aligning with the growing importance of understanding diverse cultural dynamics in technology adoption.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Travelers and Motorists Acceptance of Intelligent Transportation Applications: A SEM-ANN Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Traffic congestion is one of the biggest obstacles in the development and transformation of emerging nations. Numerous countries have implemented national smart-city programs to enhance their operations, quality of life, and competitiveness. However, there is a dearth of studies examining user behavior in relation to smart transportation services. This has sparked the need for more studies on user behavior when using intelligent transportation applications. Consequently, the goal of this study is to determine the factors crucial to the acceptance of intelligent transportation applications, thereby enabling us to understand how users will react to future traffic management technologies. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) was adopted to formulate the hypotheses of the current study. With 500 respondents, the partial least squares structural equation model (PLS-SEM) approach was used to assess both the measurement and structural models and was further verified using an artificial neural network (ANN). The findings suggest that trust and perceived usefulness are the most influential factors affecting users' intentions to adopt intelligent transportation applications.

Author Keywords: Partial Least Square Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM)

articleTitle: Dramatic Digital Communication of Internalized Misogyny: Semiotic Analysis on Pick Me Girl Content on TikTok
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Through qualitative research using Roland Barthes' semiotics analysis techniques, this study aims to identify signs of internalized misogyny in dramatic Pick Me Girl content on TikTok. Data analysis was conducted using the Internalized Misogyny Scale by Bozkur, resulting in the discovery of sixteen signs of internalized misogyny. These signs include competition, derogation, male prioritization, self-separation, internalized powerlessness, and self-objectification. By shedding light on these forms of internalized misogyny, this study hopes to foster public awareness and reduce discrimination and violence against women. Additionally, digital content creators can use these findings to create a more positive and empowering image of women. Digital technologies, including social media, should serve as tools to promote and facilitate social development for all genders in society. They should not contribute to gender inequality. In the future, it is hoped that artificial intelligence will be able to recognize gender equality and provide strategies to empower both genders while also restricting any content that promotes inequality.

articleTitle: Balance Diet Recommendation System Using Fuzzy Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: In an effort to achieve a balanced diet, it is crucial to pay attention to the proportion of the main macronutrients, namely carbohydrates, protein, and fat, in accordance with the body's needs. Unfortunately, understanding about a balanced diet is still low in Indonesia. This is a major concern as it is crucial in a child's growth and development. Therefore, the research aims to analyze the macronutrient needs of toddlers, considering age, height, and weight as the primary parameters. The results of the analysis will serve as a reference for the development of a diet recommendation system using the fuzzy Sugeno method. By employing the fuzzy method, the system can provide personalized recommendations based on individual characteristics. This research also aims to implement the diet recommendation system using a prototyping approach in the design and development process of the application. The study involves testing using MATLAB to examine the compatibility of fuzzy logic analysis results with the applied theory. To test the effectiveness of the application, a sample test was conducted on 114 toddler data, resulting in an accuracy rate of 82.5%. These findings indicate that the developed fuzzy system is capable providing diet recommendations with a high level of accuracy.

articleTitle: A Study on the Leapfrog Phenomenon in Vietnam: A Case Study of Innovation by Domestic Electric Vehicle Company
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The leapfrog phenomenon describes how the introduction of cutting-edge technologies in developing and emerging countries in such regions as Africa and Asia drive their economy and society to more advanced levels than those of Western countries, where socio-economic growth is grounded in older technologies. In Vietnam, an emerging country that has seen rapid economic growth in recent years, the introduction of electronic vehicles (EVs) by domestic manufacturer VinFast has led to nationwide innovation driven by the leapfrog phenomenon. EVs generally have an extremely small number of parts and a simple vehicle structure compared to gasoline vehicles. In addition, the company does not carry out R&D and design but concentrates on assembling and producing complete vehicles. VinFast has thus been able to bring its EVs to the market within a short period of about two years after launching its EV business. The widespread use of EVs also has enormous potential for reducing CO2 emissions. As Vietnam aims to become an environment-friendly nation, EVs are an important innovation in terms of global environmental issues as well. This paper discusses the reality and challenges of Vietnam's efforts toward innovation based on the leapfrogging model through the introduction of EVs.

articleTitle: Government Support and Consumer Acceptance of E-Wallet Payments in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to examine the effects of the eWallet on the behaviour of the Indonesian community since the Covid-19 pandemic. From 1 January to 23 January 2023 questionnaires were sent via Google Forms, which included 123 responses of respondents from public and private universities in Indonesia. The questionnaires are distributed through various social media platforms, including Line, WhatsApp and Instagram, to the respondents in use of a purposive sampling. To analyse convergent validity, discriminant validity and hypotheses testing using SmartPLS. The results show that the majority of people are changing their behaviour to adopt eWallets, which is having a significant impact on their everyday lives. Various hypotheses reflecting the demand for and interest in electronic wallets following the Covid-19 Pandemic effect, such as perceived Covid-19 risk, government support, perceived contactless and perceived usefulness, have been demonstrated. The perception of ease of use did not influence the intention to use, given that the respondents are students who are familiar with the use of technology.

articleTitle: A Cyclist Caution Spots Prediction System Using Public Road Image Data
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Cycle Tourism is becoming increasingly popular these days. However, the realization of safe cycling by knowing the caution spots in advance is often overlooked. This paper introduces an innovative system to identify caution spots by analyzing images obtained from public data. Our proposed method is a novel scoring system that quantifies the risk index using image analysis information obtained from object detection and semantic segmentation technologies. The results are visualized on maps, enabling intuitive grasping of the caution spots. The system we developed achieved an accuracy of 87.08%, precision of 62.96%, and recall of 50.00%. Although there are data source limitations, the proposed system using existing platforms provides a practical solution to provide caution spots. This technology significantly improves caution awareness, promoting proper caution and planning for safer cycling.

articleTitle: The Effect of Green Extrinsic-Intrinsic Motivation, Green Thinking, and Altruism on Green Purchasing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: A variety of problems and conditions of the current environment has taken much attention from various parties in the world: policymakers, producers, and environmental activists. On the consumer's side, increasing awareness of the environment makes them more aware and interested in choosing a friendly product. In response, researchers did more study on the characteristics that are thought to impact consumers’ intentions to buy green products, as well as the predecessors of green behavior of the individual in adopting green items (green electronics). The factors studied are green thinking, green intrinsic motivation, green altruism, and green extrinsic motivation as moderation against green purchasing intention. In this study, the questionnaire survey method collects 212 individuals in Jakarta, Indonesia, via an online questionnaire. The software for processing data is SEM analysis using SmartPLS 3.0. This research discovered that environmentally conscious thoughts, personal motivation rooted in environmental concerns, and selfless environmental behavior notably impact the intention to purchase eco-friendly electronic products. However, it was observed that external motivational factors related to environmental considerations did not play a significant role in the connection between environmentally conscious thoughts, intrinsic motivation linked to environmental values, altruistic environmental behavior, and the intention to purchase green electronic products.

articleTitle: Predicting the Use Behavior of Micro-Mobility as a Service in the Philippines: A Structural Equation Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Sustainability in transportation technologies is growing in all parts of the world through electric and micro-mobility sharing services. As such, there is a need to explore the factors that influence its adoption and use behavior. However, this is relatively underexamined in many developing countries. This study attempts to understand the intention and use behavior of micro-mobility as a service (MaaS) in the Philippines, a developing country. This study used survey data, and analysis was performed using partial least squares and structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). Results show that performance expectancy is the strongest predictor of intention, while satisfaction is the least significant predictor. Factors such as social influence, price value, and habit have a positive effect on intention. Overall, the predictive model is explained by the coefficient of determination, revealing that behavior intention, satisfaction, and use behavior have large predictive relevance. This study provides theoretical and practical implications for further micro-mobility research in the future.

Author Keywords: unified theory of acceptance and use of technology

articleTitle: Digital Fluency and its Impact on Financial Management: Pathways to Future Security and Stress Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of Current Money Management Stress (CMMS) and Expected Future Financial Security (EFFS) on Financial Stress (FS) and its impact on Financial Behaviour (FB), with Digital Knowledge (DK) as a moderating factor. Conducted with 312 participants using random sampling and PLS-SEM analysis, the study found a meaningful relationship between digital knowledge and financial behaviour, highlighting that digital literacy directly influences financial actions. Greater digital knowledge enables more advanced financial behaviour, such as proficient use of online banking and investment platforms. However, digital knowledge alone was not a significant predictor of financial stress levels, indicating that digital proficiency does not directly reduce financial stress. The research also revealed a strong link between current money management stress and overall financial stress, emphasizing the significant impact of managing current finances on financial well-being, managing day-to-day finances significantly affects overall financial stress, as observed through the strong relationship between CMMS and FS. Furthermore, a positive outlook on future financial security was associated with beneficial financial behaviour, suggesting that optimism about financial future encourages prudent financial practices. The study also found that current financial management stress influences financial behaviour, potentially leading to more cautious or poor financial choices under stress. The indirect relationship between CMMS, financial stress, and financial behaviour suggests that the effect of money management stress on behaviour is partially mediated by financial stress, indicating that stress alters financial behaviour indirectly rather than directly.

articleTitle: The Impact of Digital Financial Literacy on Savings, Expenditure, and Prospective Financial Behavior: An Exploratory Inquiry
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study examines the profound effect of Digital Financial Literacy (DFL) on financial behaviour, particularly in the context of Indonesia's rapidly expanding digital payment landscape, which has been accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic's push towards digitalisation. Using a quantitative approach and surveying 312 participants, this study delves into the influence of DFL components, including knowledge of digital financial services, financial skills, awareness of digital finance risk, and digital finance risk control, on financial goals. The findings emphasise the critical role that DFL plays in fostering responsible financial behaviours, revealing significant positive relationships between DFL components and financial goals. This study validates the essential nature of financial literacy in engaging with financial markets and services and underscores the need to incorporate digital competencies into financial education. This study contributes to the discourse on enhancing financial education in the digital age by providing a comprehensive understanding of how DFL affects spending and saving behaviours. This highlights the urgency for policymakers and educators to integrate DFL into educational programs, aiming to equip consumers with the competencies required to navigate the digital financial ecosystem safely and effectively.

articleTitle: REST API Response Time Optimization Using Elasticsearch
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study compares the performance of relational databases and unstructured databases, specifically Elasticsearch, in optimizing REST API response times. As dataset sizes increase, relational databases face prolonged data retrieval times, a common challenge for many companies relying on them for general-purpose use. Using a replica of an online coffee shop's product catalogue dataset, this research analyzes data retrieval scenarios presented in JSON format. The primary goal is to enhance REST API response times by implementing Elasticsearch, leveraging the inherent speed advantage of unstructured databases in data retrieval. The process involves replicating the catalogue data, converting it to relational JSON, setting up a Node.js server with Elasticsearch runtime, and migrating the data. The results show that Elasticsearch significantly outperforms the relational database, with an average response time of 282.6 ms compared to 754.8 ms—a 62.5596% improvement. Load testing with 200 concurrent customers accessing the REST API demonstrates a throughput of 60 requests per minute and an average response time of 930 ms, ensuring a smooth user experience under heavy demand. In conclusion, replacing relational databases with Elasticsearch optimizes data retrieval speed, emphasizing its practicality in enhancing data retrieval processes.

articleTitle: Analysis of Behavior That Influences Online Streaming Subscriptions on Music or Movie Streaming Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Technology has developed rapidly and changed the way every industry in the world works, especially in the entertainment sector, like music and movies. Over the past few years streaming subscriptions to music or movies have been growing rapidly, but there are still people who prefer to enjoy these things through piracy. Therefore, this research will focus on the factors that influence behavior in subscribing to music industry or movie industry streaming applications which will help industry growth. The population of this research is Indonesians who subscribe to music or movie streaming applications with a sample size of 358 samples. The framework used in this research consists of the variables Age, Gender, Performance Expectancy, Effort Expectancy, Social Influence, Facilitation Conditions, Hedonic Motivation, Price Value, Piracy Judgment, Habits, Usage Behavior. This research revealed that there is a correlation between variables, where most of hypotheses have a positive relationship, except for the relationship between Age and Performance Expectancy, Age and Effort Expectancy, Age and Facilitation Conditions, Age and Hedonic Motivation, Gender with Social Influence, Performance Expectancy with Usage Behavior, Effort Expectancy with Usage Behavior, Price Value with Usage Behavior which have a negative relationship.

articleTitle: The Impact of Differentiated Instruction Implementation on Science Academic Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This research aimed to explore the impact of differentiated instruction implementation on the academic performance in science subjects of primary school students. Adopting a quasi-experimental design, the study involved a systematic application of differentiated instruction in a primary school setting, contrasting the outcomes with a control group that followed traditional teaching methods. The participants comprised students from primary schools, divided into experiment group and control group. The results of the study were significant. Data analysis revealed that students who experienced the differentiated instruction exhibited notable improvements in their science academic performance compared to their counterparts in the control group. These findings were evidenced by higher scores in science subjects, reflecting a better understanding and grasp of scientific concepts and principles. The study thereby concludes that the implementation of differentiated instruction can lead to enhanced academic outcomes in science education among primary school students, advocating for its broader application in educational settings to cater to diverse learning needs.

articleTitle: Exploring the Intersection of Youth Participatory Culture, Online Opportunities and Online Risks for Sustainable Society
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This article examines youth participatory culture through the lens of digital media. Digital advances can support and accelerate the achievement of a sustainable society. Youth can take part by using technology to exchange information as well as to create their own content. This exercise exemplifies what is known as participatory culture, which has replaced consumer culture. However, this online opportunity poses an online risk. This research investigates the effect of youth participatory culture and online opportunity on online risk. A cross-sectional survey was used for online data collection (N=247). The result showed that participatory culture significantly affects online opportunity but does not affect online risk. Meanwhile, participatory culture and online opportunity simultaneously have significant effects on online risk. The results indicated that youth should participate online to obtain entertainment, learning, personal gain and commercial gain by collaborating, joining affiliation, creative expression and creating media channels.

articleTitle: Proposal for the Support Method Presentation Model Utilizing Nursing Home Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: One of the significant problems faced by dementia group homes is the high caregiver turnover rate. In particular, there is an urgent need to prevent the turnover of new caregivers and work toward ensuring and improving the quality of care. To address this issue, we are developing a care method support system that utilizes two databases: a personal attributes database and a care case database ([1]–[3]). The personal attributes database extracts personal attributes such as hobbies and previous occupations of residents from care records and care conference minutes. The care case database extracts cases of resident problems, their solutions, and the original text containing them. The care method support system presents candidates for appropriate responses to problems faced by residents based on these databases. In this study, we generated two care suggestion models: Care Suggestion Model: This model applies text similarity to the care case database to suggest candidates for appropriate responses to unregistered problems. Personalized Care Suggestion Model: This model applies clustering to the personal attributes database and generates a care suggestion model that considers personal attributes. We compared the two models and tested the usefulness of the model.

Author Keywords: Data Base of nursing Care Cases

articleTitle: Improving Organizational Performance (Student Club at One of Private University in Indonesia) Through Digital Leadership Mediated by Digital Skills
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: The primary objective is to investigate the role of digital leadership as mediated by digital skills in improving organizational performance in accordance with a quarterly evaluation program of student club leaders at one of the best private universities in Indonesia based on Qs World University Ranking 2024. The sample size for this study was 166 participants, including members of the general president and regional president of student club leaders at One Private University in Indonesia. The Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) technique was used to test the link between variables and hypotheses. According to hypothesis testing results, digital leadership has significant effects on organizational performance and digital skills. In the meanwhile, Digital Skill has a positve but insignificant impact on Organizational Performance. There is no influence of the indirect correlation between Digital Leadership and Organizational Performance via Digital Skills.

articleTitle: Unravelling the Determinants of Heritage Tourism Experience Sharing Intentions on Social Media: A Jakarta-Centric Study
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This paper examines cultural tourism in Jakarta and travellers' willingness to share their experiences on social media. Social media marketing for tourist sites can be learned from the study. Researchers use the Technology Acceptance Model to understand visitors' mindsets and plans. A Jakarta quantitative survey included 165 people. The findings demonstrate that tourists who visit historic places are more inclined to write about their experiences on social media if they find it useful, easy to use, and favourable. Travellers' objectives and opinions must be considered while building destination marketing social media strategy. The paper says social media affects historical travellers' decisions. Trusted friends and family's social media posts influence visitors' decisions. Cultural heritage-based tourism and social media's impact on destination marketing are also examined. The study is limited in sample size and generalizability but provides valuable information. Future studies should broaden the scope and include other perspectives to comprehend travellers' social media sharing of historic tourism experiences. Finally, this study examines how historic visitors plan to share their experiences on social media to add to the literature. The findings show how Jakarta, Indonesia, and other tourism destinations might use social media to attract and engage tourists.

articleTitle: Benefits of using a Tablet Solely for Teaching and Learning Sessions at school
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: Nowadays, technology has revolutionized numerous industries, including education. As a result, the use of tablets for teaching and assessment in the classroom has greatly increased. It has enhanced students’ learning effectiveness. This study focuses on justifying the problems faced by the students during the learning and teaching sessions. A survey method using a Google form questionnaire was used to collect data from students, and 54 respondents answered the survey. The study results showed that 57.4% of the respondents felt that the books in their bags during primary or secondary school were very heavy, and 53.7% of them had a very high awareness of heavy bags on physical health. Therefore, Hypnota was created to address all issues and benefit teachers and students. Hypnota is a tablet-sized device designed solely for learning and teaching sessions in school. Since it helps teachers provide tailored resources, activities, and support as needed, Hypnota can be an excellent tool for teaching multi-level classrooms.

articleTitle: Human Capital Development of Thai Expatriates in Japan and Its Influence on Technological Development in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This paper aims to determine the human capital Thai returnees gained from Japan and how the returnees contributed to technology development in Thailand. To achieve the objective, 60 Thai entrepreneurs and managers who went to Japan during 1984 to 2020 were surveyed using a questionnaire supported with 26 in-depth interviews. The survey results indicated that Thai returnees from Japan improved technical skills, managerial skills (mainly teamwork, 5S, Kaizen, Quality Circles, Ho-ren-son), Japanese language, and work ethics (mainly responsibility, punctuality, hard work, eagerness to learn, discipline and obeying rules). The human capital helped the firms to reach ‘transformation’ and ‘exploitation’, stages of the absorptive capacity indicating their capability to adapt and utilize Japanese advanced technology. As a result, their firms have reached the “creative imitation” stage of technological development implying that they managed to add new features to the imitated technologies/products from Japan. In conclusion, while supporting human capital development by dispatching more students and workforce to Japan, new policy directions will be necessary to promote returnee innovations in Thai firms.

articleTitle: Quiz Magus: Customized Game-Based Assessment for E-Learning with Data Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: This study aims to develop a platform to help educators to create a customizable game-based assessment for evaluating students' academic knowledge on a subject and having the ability to easily manage these results more efficiently. This study is motivated by traditional assessment has been the standard norm for students and being able to provide an alternative method in terms of assessment taking would help improve the students' experience in assessment taking in terms of engagement and interactivity through gamification. The game-based assessment platform was then evaluated by students and educators under the ISO 9126 criteria, it was then able to score an overall mean of 4.7 with a verbal interpretation of “Excellent” which shows that the system was able to deliver the needs of the users and they were able to conduct their assessments within the platform with little or no issue. The proposed system can also provide an easier way of data gathering results from students with the use of the system's data visualization and reporting capabilities. Overall, the system is acceptable to the students and experts' evaluators. This indicates that the system is able to facilitate the learning process and assessment in an effective and efficient manner with less human effort needed while providing student centered learning environment. Implications for practice are offered.

articleTitle: AI Models for Defect Detection in Lean Manufacturing: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Business and Industrial Research (ICBIR)
abstract: In this comparative study, we evaluate deep learning techniques for defect detection within lean manufacturing settings. Our methodical literature review identified key deep learning architectures—CNNs, R-CNNs, and YOLO variants—for their track record in accurate defect identification. Employing a standardized dataset, models were assessed against lean manufacturing criteria: accuracy, precision, recall, and processing speed. The analysis revealed that while DCNNs offer high precision in detecting surface defects, R-CNNs decrease false negatives, vital for production reliability. Models like FCNNs show promise for rapid defect recognition, an essential component for maintaining manufacturing throughput. Our findings suggest these techniques can significantly contribute to the goals of lean manufacturing by enhancing defect detection and optimizing quality control processes. Future research should continue to refine AI model integration and scalability within varied manufacturing environments, emphasizing adaptability and efficiency to support lean manufacturing principles. This study provides a foundational understanding of AI's potential in improving defect detection, a step towards integrating cutting-edge technology in manufacturing systems for enhanced quality assurance and waste reduction.
